paths.title: MS-102 Configure your Microsoft 365 tenant
paths.summary: This learning path provides instruction on how to configure your Microsoft 365 tenant, including your organizational profile, tenant subscriptions, user accounts and licenses, groups, custom domains, and client connectivity.

modules.title: Configure your Microsoft 365 experience
modules.learnSummary: This module examines each of the tasks that an organization must complete to successfully configure its Microsoft 365 experience.
modules.tldr: Buying a Microsoft 365 subscription creates a Microsoft Entra tenant: the container for users, domains and settings, hosted in a datacenter region fixed at sign-up. This module covers the first configuration tasks: organization profile and themes, licenses and billing, add-on services, SharePoint/OneDrive and Teams tenant settings, unified audit logging and a final readiness checklist.
objectives: Configure your company’s organization profile, which is essential for setting up for your company’s tenant.
Maintain minimum subscription requirements for your company.
Manage your services and add-ins by assigning more licenses, purchasing more storage, and so on.
Create a checklist that enables you to confirm your Microsoft Entra tenant meets your business needs.
keyPoints: A **subscription** is paid access to a **plan** (E3, E5…); the so-called "Microsoft 365 tenant" is technically a **Microsoft Entra tenant** — one tenant per subscription; more tenants mean more subscriptions.
The tenant URL comes from the name chosen at sign-up (`contoso.onmicrosoft.com`); the **country/region** can never be changed — moving it means a **new account and new subscription**.
The **Preferred language** controls Microsoft's communications; changing it later doesn't change the **SharePoint** language set at sign-up.
Themes: one **default theme** plus up to **four custom themes**, assigned to **Microsoft 365 groups** only (not security or distribution groups); only Global Administrators can customize them.
Too few **licenses** causes provisioning errors, too many wastes money; licenses and subscriptions are managed under **Billing** in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
SharePoint/OneDrive external sharing is set at **organization level** in the SharePoint admin center; sites and OneDrive can only be **equally or more restrictive**.
**Unified audit logging** is on by default, retains Audit (Standard) data **180 days** (extendable up to 10 years with retention policies) and is searched in the **Microsoft Purview portal**.
Finish setup with a **checklist** (domains, sync, MFA, Conditional Access, Intune, DLP…) and verify with **Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer** and the **Get Help** app (formerly SARA).

units.title: Explore your Microsoft 365 cloud environment
points: Plan = set of features (E3, E5); subscription = ongoing paid access to a plan, usually with multiple licenses.
Purchasing a plan creates a Microsoft Entra tenant that provides authentication and authorization for Microsoft 365 services; combining plans (e.g. Microsoft 365 E5 + EMS E5) still yields one tenant.
Licensing flow: choose the plan → buy the number of seats → assign licenses in the Microsoft 365 admin center → add or remove as needs change.
Multiple tenants require multiple subscriptions — common for different user needs, licensing flexibility, compliance or mergers and acquisitions.

A well-designed tenant has the right products and licenses, correct DNS domains and network optimization, directory sync, MFA/passwordless and Conditional Access, and device management via Intune or Basic Mobility and Security.

units.title: Configure your Microsoft 365 organizational profile
points: Edit under **Settings > Org settings > Organization profile**; requires Global Administrator. An incomplete address halts provisioning.
Country/region determines available services, taxes and billing currency and datacenter location — it can't be changed.
Themes: default theme (can't be renamed, applies to everyone) plus up to four group themes, each mapped to up to five Microsoft 365 groups; users in several themed groups see the default theme.
Theme tabs: General (name, groups), Logos (HTTPS, anonymously accessible URL; uploaded default logo under 10 KB), Colors (navigation bar, text/icon, accent).

units.title: Manage your tenant subscriptions in Microsoft 365
points: Review licenses under **Billing > Licenses > Subscriptions**; assign, remove and buy extra licenses there.
Extra licenses bought later get their own monthly billing date.
Billing pages: Purchase services, Your products, Licenses, Bills and payments, Billing accounts, Payment methods, Billing notifications.

units.title: Integrate Microsoft 365 with customer engagement apps
points: **Purchase services** (under Billing) buys new products and add-ons (e.g. Project Online, Power BI), often with a 30-day trial, and lets you compare products side by side.
Assign an add-on by licensing the user from the Users page, or via **Assign to** after claiming the license.
**Private Azure Marketplace** is a tenant-level governance layer: only approved ISV apps can be deployed; Microsoft apps and endorsed Linux distributions are approved by default.
Setup: assign the Marketplace admin role → create the private marketplace (disabled, with a Default Collection that can't be renamed or deleted) → add collections → enable it.

units.title: Configure tenant-level sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive
points: External sharing is **on by default**; configure it in **SharePoint admin center > Policies > Sharing** (Global or SharePoint Administrator). The most restrictive of org and site settings applies.
Four levels: Anyone (default), New and existing guests, Existing guests, Only people in your organization. Turning sharing off removes guest access within about an hour.
More settings: limit sharing by domain (up to 5000 domains, or `Set-SPOTenant`), allow only specific security groups to share externally, guest access expiration, verification-code reauthentication.
Default link type (Specific people / Only people in your organization / Anyone with the link) and Anyone-link expiration and view-only permission can be set.
Microsoft Entra external collaboration settings also control who can invite guests.

units.title: Configure tenant-level settings for Microsoft Teams
points: Organization-level areas in the Teams admin center: guest access, Teams upgrade (coexistence modes such as Islands or Teams Only), Teams settings (policies), Teams apps, analytics and reports.

**Meeting policies** are assigned to users, groups or the whole org and control features like private meeting scheduling, Meet now in channels, video, screen sharing, transcription, cloud recording and live captions.
**Meeting settings** apply to all meetings: presenter role mode, who can bypass the lobby, dial-in lobby bypass, anonymous join, private chat, reactions, shared notes.
App permission policies allow or block apps; app setup policies pin and preinstall apps.

units.title: Enable Unified Audit Logging in Microsoft 365
points: Records user and admin activity across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Power BI, Microsoft Entra ID and more; searched in the Microsoft Purview portal.
On by default; verify in **Exchange Online PowerShell** with `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled` (in Security & Compliance PowerShell it always shows False).
Turn on via the Purview **Audit** banner or `Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true`; needs the **Audit Logs** role; results can take about an hour.
Turning auditing off also blocks the Office 365 Management Activity API and Microsoft Sentinel from audit data.
Audit retention policies can extend the default 180 days up to 10 years; searches can be exported to CSV.

units.title: Complete your tenant configuration in Microsoft 365
points: Checklist: user and mailbox migration, permissions, custom domains, Intune enrollment and co-management, mobile governance, DNS and mail flow, Microsoft Entra Connect Sync, MFA.
Also: Conditional Access, block legacy authentication, audit logging, DLP and information protection, Microsoft Secure Score, periodic security reviews.

Verify readiness with **Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer** (DNS and mail flow) and the **Get Help** app (connectivity issues; some older Learn units still name the Microsoft Support and Recovery Assistant, SARA).
Tenant-to-tenant migration (mergers, acquisitions) is out of scope for this module.

keyTerms.definition: The container created with a Microsoft 365 subscription that holds users, domains and settings and provides identity services.
A plan is a feature set (E3, E5); a subscription is the recurring paid access to that plan, with a number of licenses.
Tenant-wide company details (name, address, preferred language, country/region) and themes in Org settings.
Tenant-level control over which third-party (ISV) Azure Marketplace apps users can deploy, using collections.
Teams settings for meeting features assigned to users, groups or the whole organization.
Central record of user and admin activities across Microsoft 365 services, searched in Microsoft Purview.

tables.title: SharePoint and OneDrive external sharing levels
rows: Unauthenticated Anyone links plus sharing with guests; links can be forced to expire or be view-only. Required for file requests.
Guests must sign in (work/school or Microsoft account) or use a verification code; new guests can be invited.
Only guests already in the directory.
External sharing off; guests lose access within about an hour.

remember: Headquarters moved to another country → **new account and new subscription**, not an edit of the org profile or a support call.
Custom themes target **Microsoft 365 groups**, never security or distribution groups; max **5 themes** in total.
Org vs site sharing conflict → the **most restrictive** wins; OneDrive can never be more permissive than SharePoint.
Check audit status in **Exchange Online PowerShell** — Security & Compliance PowerShell always reports False.

selfCheck.q: A company's Microsoft 365 tenant was set up with France as country/region, but HQ moved to the US. How do you change it?
selfCheck.a: You can't edit it: sign up for a new account with the United States as country/region and purchase a new subscription.

selfCheck.q: The sales team needs a different suite header theme from everyone else. What do you configure?
selfCheck.a: A custom group theme in Org settings > Organization profile > Custom themes, assigned to the sales team's Microsoft 365 group.

selfCheck.q: Audit log searches return nothing. How do you check and fix this with PowerShell?
selfCheck.a: In Exchange Online PowerShell run `Get-AdminAuditLogConfig` and check `UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled`; if False, run `Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true`.

modules.title: Manage users, licenses, guests, and contacts in Microsoft 365
modules.learnSummary: This module provides instruction on how to create and manage user accounts, assign Microsoft 365 licenses to users, recover deleted user accounts, and create and manage guests and contacts.
modules.tldr: Users in Microsoft 365 are cloud, synchronized or federated identities; that model decides where you create and manage them. Accounts are created in the Microsoft 365 admin center, by CSV import, with Microsoft Graph PowerShell or by directory sync, and need a usage location and a license before they can use services. Deleted users can be restored for 30 days, guests join via Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration, and external people who only need email become mail contacts.
objectives: Identify which user identity model best suited for your organization.
Create user accounts from both the Microsoft 365 admin center and Windows PowerShell.
Manage user accounts and licenses in Microsoft 365.
Recover deleted user accounts in Microsoft 365.
Perform bulk user maintenance in Microsoft Entra ID.
Create and manage guests and collaborate with them in SharePoint sites.
Create and manage contacts.
keyPoints: Three identity models: **cloud** (only in Microsoft Entra ID), **synchronized** (on-prem AD DS is the source, synced by Microsoft Entra Connect Sync or Cloud Sync) and **federated** (authentication redirected to a trusted IdP such as AD FS).
With directory sync, synced users are **mastered on-premises**: create and edit them with AD tools, not the Microsoft 365 admin center (which can still set location and licenses).
**Microsoft Graph PowerShell** replaces the deprecated Azure AD, Azure AD Preview and MSOnline modules (`New-MgUser`, `Set-MgUserLicense`).
A license can only be assigned when **UsageLocation** is set (ISO two-letter code); synced accounts have no location by default.
Removing a license deletes the user's service data after a **30-day grace period**; deleted users are **soft-deleted for 30 days** and can be restored (deleted **security groups** can't).
Microsoft Entra admin center **bulk operations** use CSV templates: create (UPN, name, password, block sign-in), delete (UPN) and restore (**object ID**).
Guests are **B2B collaboration** users with UserType **Guest** and `#EXT#` in their UPN; Microsoft Entra external collaboration settings **override** sharing settings in Microsoft 365.
**Mail contacts** are external addresses visible in the **GAL** without a user account; mail users have an address in your own domain.

units.title: Determine the user identity model for your organization
points: Cloud identity: exists only in Microsoft Entra ID; a same-named on-prem account isn't linked and has its own password. Simple, typical for small organizations.
Synchronized identity: AD DS is authoritative; authentication happens in the cloud unless **Pass-through Authentication (PTA)** sends it to on-prem AD.

Federated identity: Microsoft Entra ID redirects sign-in to a trusted IdP (e.g. AD FS) via relying party trust and metadata exchange; main benefit is **single sign-on**, and on-prem password and lockout policies apply.
Federation depends on on-prem availability — an internet outage can break Microsoft 365 sign-in; mitigate by hosting AD DS and AD FS in Azure.

units.title: Create user accounts in Microsoft 365
points: Methods: Microsoft 365 admin center (or admin app), **Add multiple users** with a CSV, Microsoft Graph PowerShell, or directory synchronization.
Admin center wizard (Users > Active users > Add a user): basics and password → product licenses → optional roles → review.
PowerShell: `Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.ReadWrite.All'`, then `New-MgUser` with UPN, display name, `-PasswordProfile`, `-AccountEnabled` and `-MailNickName`.
In synced environments, create users with Active Directory Users and Computers or `New-ADUser`; they reach Microsoft Entra ID through sync.

units.title: Manage user account settings in Microsoft 365
points: Cloud-only users are managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center, PowerShell or Microsoft Entra admin center; hybrid users with on-prem AD DS tools.
A Microsoft 365 subscription includes the Free edition of Microsoft Entra ID; Premium P1/P2 add more features.
An unlicensed account can open the admin center but can't use any services until it has a location and license.

User pane tabs: Account (aliases, groups, roles, MFA, sign out of all sessions, 30-day sign-in history), Devices, Licenses and Apps (location, apps), Mail (permissions, forwarding, litigation hold), OneDrive.

units.title: Manage user licenses in Microsoft 365
points: Only **Global Administrators** and **User Administrators** can assign or remove licenses; assigning sets up the service automatically.
See remaining licenses in Billing > Licenses; filter Active users on **Unlicensed users**. Bulk options: **Replace**, **Assign more**, **Unassign all**.

PowerShell: `Get-MgSubscribedSku` (available = ActiveUnits − WarningUnits − ConsumedUnits); find unlicensed users with `assignedLicenses/$count eq 0`; set location with `Update-MgUser -UsageLocation`.
`Set-MgUserLicense -AddLicenses @{SkuId=...}` assigns a SKU; `DisabledPlans` turns off individual service plans (e.g. Bookings, Sway). `Get-MgUser` without `-All` returns only 100 users.

units.title: Recover deleted user accounts in Microsoft 365
points: Deleting a user frees the license; delete in Active users or with `Remove-MgUser -UserId`.
The account is soft-deleted and restorable for **30 days** from Users > **Deleted users** > Restore user (choose how to set the password).
PowerShell: `Restore-MgDirectoryDeletedItem -DirectoryObjectId` restores users, groups, apps, service principals and administrative units.
Deleted **security groups** are permanently deleted and can't be recovered.

units.title: Perform bulk user maintenance in Microsoft Entra ID
points: Microsoft Entra admin center > Users > **Bulk operations**: Bulk create, Bulk delete; Deleted users > **Bulk restore**. Requires Global Administrator or User Administrator.
Each operation has its own CSV template: don't change the first two rows (version, headings), replace the example row, avoid extra columns and whitespace.
Required values: create = Name, UPN, Initial password, Block sign in; delete = UPN; restore = **Object ID**.
Check progress and error files on **Bulk operation results**; one create job runs up to an hour (at least 50,000 users).
PowerShell alternative: `Import-Csv | foreach { New-MgUser ... }` and export results to a CSV.

units.title: Create and manage guest users using B2B collaboration
points: B2B collaboration (Microsoft Entra External ID) lets external users sign in with their own credentials; they get a user object with UserType Guest and `#EXT#` in the UPN.
UserType (Guest/Member) describes the relationship only; **Identities** shows the IdP (ExternalAzureAD, Microsoft account, google.com, mail = email one-time passcode, issuer URI for SAML/WS-Fed).
Guest permission levels: Same as member users, **Limited access (default)**, Restricted access (only own profile). No license needed to restrict.

External collaboration settings control who can invite (by default all users, including guests), self-service sign-up and allowed/blocked domains; inviting requires e.g. Guest Inviter or User Administrator.
Invite via Users > New user > **Invite external user**; status is PendingAcceptance until redeemed; invitations don't expire. Guests can be added to groups and enterprise apps.

units.title: Collaborate with guests in a SharePoint site
points: Step 1: Microsoft Entra external collaboration settings must allow guest invites and not block the guest domain — they override Microsoft 365 settings.
Step 2: Org settings > Microsoft 365 Groups: allow owners to add guests **and** let guests access group content.
Step 3: SharePoint org-level sharing set to **Anyone** or **New and existing guests**; site settings can't be more permissive.
Steps 4–6: create the team site, check its site-level sharing, then add people through the site's **Microsoft 365 group** membership.

units.title: Create and manage contacts
points: Mail contacts are mail-enabled objects with an external address, shown in the GAL; mail users have an address in your domain.
Create in Users > **Contacts** (Global Administrator, Exchange Administrator or Directory Writers); option to hide from the GAL; allow 30 minutes to take effect.
The admin center can't bulk edit or delete contacts — use the classic EAC or Exchange Online PowerShell.
PowerShell: `New-MailContact`, `Set-Contact` (organization info), `Set-MailContact` (mail properties, e.g. hide from address lists), `Remove-MailContact`.

keyTerms.definition: User account that exists only in Microsoft Entra ID, with its own password.
On-prem AD DS account synced to Microsoft Entra ID; AD DS is the source of authority.
Synced account whose authentication is redirected to a trusted IdP such as AD FS, giving SSO.
Synced users' passwords are validated directly against on-prem Active Directory.
ISO country/region code on a user that must be set before a license can be assigned.
Microsoft Entra External ID feature that invites external users to sign in with their own credentials as guests.
Mail-enabled object for an external email address, visible in the GAL, with no user account.

tables.title: Identity models
rows: Small and medium organizations, or those no longer needing AD DS
On-prem AD DS, synced to the cloud
Organizations with AD DS moving to the cloud
Same sign-in, identities managed in one place
Synced, authenticated by AD FS or another IdP
Centralized authentication or special sign-in (e.g. ID cards)
Single sign-on, identities managed in one place

tables.title: Guest user access levels in Microsoft Entra ID
rows: Only their own profile; no group memberships

remember: "Can't assign a license" to a synced user → check **UsageLocation** first.
Bulk restore needs the **object ID**, bulk delete needs the **UPN**.
Guest sharing blocked even though SharePoint allows it → **Microsoft Entra external collaboration settings** win.
External person only needs to appear in the GAL for email → **mail contact**, not a guest or user account.

selfCheck.q: A user left and you removed their Microsoft 365 E3 license. What happens to their service data?
selfCheck.a: It's deleted, but you have a 30-day grace period to recover it; after that it's gone.

selfCheck.q: Contoso uses directory sync. An admin tries to create a new employee in the Microsoft 365 admin center. What should they do instead?
selfCheck.a: Create the account on-premises (Active Directory Users and Computers or `New-ADUser`) and let Microsoft Entra Connect Sync or Cloud Sync sync it.

selfCheck.q: Guests from several partner companies shouldn't see each other or any group memberships. Which setting do you choose?
selfCheck.a: Set guest user access to Restricted access in the Microsoft Entra external collaboration settings, so guests see only their own profile.

modules.title: Manage groups in Microsoft 365
modules.learnSummary: This module provides instruction on how to create groups for distributing email to multiple users within Exchange Online. It also explains how to create groups to support collaboration in SharePoint Online.
modules.tldr: Microsoft 365 has several group types: Microsoft 365 groups for collaboration, distribution and dynamic distribution groups for email, security groups for permissions, mail-enabled security groups for both, and shared mailboxes. Groups can be created in several admin centers or with Microsoft Graph PowerShell. Microsoft Entra ID adds dynamic membership rules, group-based licensing and a naming policy for Microsoft 365 groups.
objectives: Describe the various types of groups available in Microsoft 365.
Create and manage groups using the Microsoft 365 admin center and Windows PowerShell.
Create and manage groups in Exchange Online and SharePoint Online.
keyPoints: **Microsoft 365 group** = the recommended type: group mailbox plus shared workspace (calendar, SharePoint team site, Planner…); creating a **team** creates one behind the scenes.
**Security group** = permissions only; **distribution group** = email only; **mail-enabled security group** = both, but it can't be dynamic or contain devices.

**Dynamic distribution groups** are Exchange-only and recalculate recipients every **24 hours**; **dynamic membership** in Microsoft Entra ID works for security and Microsoft 365 groups and needs **Microsoft Entra ID P1** per member.
Only deleted **Microsoft 365 groups** can be restored (30-day soft delete), together with their mailbox, site, Planner and team; other group types are gone for good.
**Group-based licensing** assigns licenses to members automatically and removes them when they leave; it doesn't support **nested** groups (only first-level members get licenses).
Synced on-prem groups must be edited with **local Active Directory tools**, not the Microsoft 365 admin center.
The **naming policy** (prefix/suffix and up to 5000 blocked words) applies only to **Microsoft 365 groups**, is configured in the Microsoft Entra admin center and needs P1 per member.
Manage team membership **in Teams**; changes made elsewhere can take up to **24 hours** to appear in Teams.

units.title: Examine groups in Microsoft 365
points: Six options: Microsoft 365 group, distribution group, mail-enabled security group, security group, dynamic distribution group (Exchange admin center only) and shared mailbox.

A Microsoft 365 group can include a shared inbox and calendar, SharePoint team site and library, Planner and Power BI; a team or Viva Engage group if created from those apps. Teams and Viva Engage can't share the same group.
Group mailboxes of teams created in Teams are hidden by default; show them with `Set-UnifiedGroup -HiddenFromExchangeClientsEnabled`.
Someone removed from a group keeps team chat for about two hours; deleting a group marks its SharePoint site for deletion.

units.title: Create and manage groups in Microsoft 365
points: Best practices: clear naming, at least **two owners**, put users in security groups and add those groups to SharePoint groups or roles.

Create in Groups > Active groups > Add a group (type, basics, owners, settings such as public/private and creating a team) or with `New-MgGroup`; check types in the **Type** column or with `Get-MgGroup`.
Nesting is limited: Microsoft 365 groups can't be members of any group; security groups can only be nested in security groups.

Group-based licensing needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 (or e.g. Microsoft 365 E3 / Business Premium) and enough licenses for every member; manage it in Billing > Licenses or with `Set-MgGroupLicense`. Service plans can be disabled per group.
A license assigned from multiple sources is consumed only once.

units.title: Create dynamic groups using Microsoft Entra rule builder
points: Membership type **Dynamic user** or **Dynamic device**; a rule can't mix users and devices, and device rules can't use the owner's user attributes. Members can't be added manually.
The rule builder handles up to **five expressions**; use the rule syntax text box for more, for Direct Reports, operator precedence or complex `-any`/`-all` rules.
Syntax: `Property Operator Value`, e.g. `user.department -eq "Sales"`; operators include `-eq`, `-contains`, `-match` (regex) and `-in`; max 3072 characters.
Common rules: all users `user.objectId -ne null` (add `user.userType -eq "Member"` to exclude guests), all devices `device.objectId -ne null`, and `Direct Reports for "<manager objectID>"`.
extensionAttribute1–15 and custom extension properties (`user.extension_[GUID]_[Attribute]`) are supported; multi-value extension properties aren't.

units.title: Create a Microsoft 365 group naming policy
points: Applies to user-created Microsoft 365 groups in every workload (Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Planner…), to both name and alias; not to Exchange distribution groups.
Prefix/suffix can be fixed strings or attributes: [Department], [Company], [Office], [StateOrProvince], [CountryOrRegion], [Title]; keep prefixes and suffixes under 53 characters in total.
Custom blocked words: up to 5000, case-insensitive, exact match only (no substring search).
Exempt roles include Global Administrator, Partner Tier 1/2 Support and User Administrator.
Configure in Microsoft Entra admin center > Groups > Group settings > **Naming policy**.

units.title: Create groups in Exchange Online and SharePoint Online
points: The Exchange admin center creates Microsoft 365, distribution, mail-enabled security and dynamic distribution groups.
Distribution and mail-enabled security groups show in the Microsoft 365 admin center and can be deleted there, but can only be **edited in the Exchange admin center**.
SharePoint creates default groups per site (e.g. Visitors, Members, Owners) based on the site template, using default permission levels.
A Microsoft Entra security group works across Microsoft 365; a SharePoint group only within its site. You can't email a regular security group, only a mail-enabled one.

keyTerms.definition: Membership object in Microsoft Entra ID linked to a shared mailbox, calendar, SharePoint site, Planner and optionally a team.
Security group with an email address, used for both permissions and mail distribution.
Exchange Online group whose recipients are recalculated every 24 hours from filters.
Microsoft Entra rule on user or device attributes that adds and removes members automatically.
Assigning product licenses to a group so members get them automatically.
Prefix/suffix and blocked-word rules enforced on user-created Microsoft 365 groups.

tables.title: Which group type?
rows: Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft Entra admin center, Exchange admin center, Outlook
Microsoft 365 admin center, Exchange admin center
Microsoft 365 admin center, Exchange admin center
Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft Entra admin center
Several people use one mailbox (e.g. support)
Microsoft 365 admin center, Exchange admin center

remember: Shared workspace for email, files and calendar → **Microsoft 365 group**, not a distribution or security group.
Restore a deleted group → only possible for **Microsoft 365 groups**, within 30 days.
Dynamic *distribution* group = Exchange filters; dynamic *membership* group = Microsoft Entra rules and **P1** licenses.
Naming policy blocks only **exact** word matches and never affects Exchange distribution groups.

selfCheck.q: A security group is synced from on-prem AD with Microsoft Entra Connect Sync. Where do you change its membership?
selfCheck.a: In the local Active Directory management tools; the Microsoft 365 admin center can't edit synced groups.

selfCheck.q: You need a group containing every employee but no guests, maintained automatically. What rule do you use?
selfCheck.a: A dynamic user group with `(user.objectId -ne null) -and (user.userType -eq "Member")`.

selfCheck.q: You assign Microsoft 365 E3 to a group that contains another group. Which users get a license?
selfCheck.a: Only the first-level members; group-based licensing doesn't support nested groups.

modules.title: Add a custom domain in Microsoft 365
modules.learnSummary: This module provides instruction on how to add a custom domain to your Microsoft 365 deployment. It also examines the DNS requirements that are necessary to support a new domain.
modules.tldr: Adding a custom domain replaces `onmicrosoft.com` addresses with your own domain. You plan the domains, a publicly available DNS zone and the DNS records each service needs. Then you prove ownership with a TXT (or MX) record and add MX, CNAME, SPF and SRV records to connect Exchange Online, Teams and other services.
objectives: Identify the factors that must be considered when adding a custom domain to Microsoft 365.
Plan the DNS zones used in a custom domain.
Plan the DNS record requirements for a custom domain.
Add a custom domain to your Microsoft 365 deployment.
keyPoints: Up to **5,000 domains** per subscription; add the **root domain before subdomains**; Business Premium and Enterprise plans support subdomains.
You need DNS console access to add **A, CNAME, TXT, MX and SRV** records — otherwise ask the DNS hosting provider to make the changes.
The DNS zone must be **publicly available** for verification, mail delivery and Autodiscover; same internal and external zone name = **split DNS** (split brain DNS).
Verify ownership with a **TXT record** (`MS=ms########`, recommended) or, if the registrar can't do TXT, a temporary **MX record**.
Changing the **MX record** to `<MX token>.mail.protection.outlook.com` sends **all** new mail for the domain to Microsoft 365 — create the users first.
Only **one SPF record** per domain (`v=spf1 include:spf.protection.outlook.com -all`), max **10 DNS lookups**; then add **DKIM and DMARC**.
Add the custom domain **before adding users** so you don't set them up twice.

units.title: Plan a custom domain for your Microsoft 365 deployment
points: Add the main domain plus every other domain used for email (business groups, mergers).
Subdomains (e.g. `sales.adatum.com`) are supported in Business Premium and Enterprise plans; register the root domain first.
DNS can be hosted on your own servers or by an external provider; you need rights to add A, CNAME, TXT, MX and SRV records.
Sometimes a domain is deliberately not registered (e.g. a university keeping faculty on-prem and students in Microsoft 365 with another domain), or not all records point to Microsoft 365.

units.title: Plan the DNS zones for a custom domain
points: A public DNS zone is required for domain verification, MX records, Autodiscover and federation records; protect it with DNSSEC and access controls.
Hybrid planning: namespace integration, DNS forwarding, split DNS, synchronization of records, service discovery (SRV), monitoring.
Different names (e.g. `adatum.local` inside): internal DNS forwards external queries to an external DNS server.
Same name (**split DNS**): internal and external servers return different IPs for the same host — both zones need the records the setup wizard requests.
Cloud-only: choose a DNS provider (e.g. Azure DNS), design zone hierarchy and delegation, use DNSSEC.

units.title: Plan the DNS record requirements for a custom domain
points: Core: **TXT** verification record for all customers; the `msoid` CNAME is only for Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet in China (elsewhere it breaks license activation).
Exchange Online: **CNAME** `autodiscover` → `autodiscover.outlook.com`, **MX** with the lowest priority number, **SPF** TXT; Exchange federation adds extra TXT and CNAME records.
Teams (Teams-only tenants): SRV `_sipfederationtls._tcp` → `sipfed.online.lync.com:5061`, SRV `_sip._tls` → `sipdir.online.lync.com:443`, CNAME `lyncdiscover` → `webdir.online.lync.com`.
Some providers (e.g. GoDaddy) can configure the records automatically, or Microsoft 365 can host the DNS records.
SPF is built from `v=spf1` + includes or `ip4`/`ip6` for other mail systems + `-all`.

units.title: Create a custom domain in Microsoft 365
points: Public WHOIS often no longer shows the registrant; use historical WHOIS, the registrar, transfer documentation or legal help to prove ownership.

**Settings > Domains**: add the TXT record (`MS=ms########`, TTL 3600) and select **Verify** — usually about 15 minutes. MX verification needs a unique, unused priority value and must be removed afterwards.
Then add the MX record (priority 0, then remove other MX records), CNAME records (Teams, Exchange Online, MDM), the SPF TXT and SRV records from the setup wizard.
Exchange Online supports TTL values under 6 hours; if SPF already exists, **merge** the Microsoft 365 values into the single record.
If the provider lacks SRV fields, combine service and protocol in Name (`_sip._tls`) and priority/weight/port/target in Target (`100 1 443 sipdir.online.lync.com`).

keyTerms.definition: Internal and external DNS zones with the same name returning different IP addresses for the same host.
`MS=ms…` value from the admin center that proves domain ownership; doesn't affect other services.
Tells other mail systems where to deliver mail for the domain; for Exchange Online it points to `*.mail.protection.outlook.com`.
`autodiscover` → `autodiscover.outlook.com`, lets Outlook find and configure Exchange Online automatically.
TXT record listing the servers allowed to send mail for the domain; one per domain, max 10 lookups.
Service location record used for Teams/Skype for Business SIP and federation.

tables.title: Main DNS records for Microsoft 365
rows: Skype for Business Online phones in Teams-only tenants
PowerShell cmdlets still using Skype for Business Online

remember: Registrar can't create TXT records → verify with an **MX record**, then delete it.
Already have SPF for another mail system → **edit the existing record**, never add a second SPF record.
Internal and external zones with the same name → **split DNS**, with the Microsoft 365 records in both zones.
`msoid` CNAME outside 21Vianet China → users get "isn't in our system" and can't activate licenses.

selfCheck.q: You want to add `sales.adatum.com` to Microsoft 365, but `adatum.com` isn't added yet. What must happen first?
selfCheck.a: Add and verify the root domain `adatum.com`; root domains must be added before subdomains.

selfCheck.q: Users already have mail at the domain with another provider. What should you do before switching the MX record?
selfCheck.a: Create their accounts in Microsoft 365 first, because after the MX change all new mail for the domain goes to Microsoft 365.

selfCheck.q: Mail from your domain sent through Exchange Online and an on-prem relay is being flagged as spoofed. How should SPF look?
selfCheck.a: One SPF TXT record: `v=spf1`, `include:spf.protection.outlook.com`, the on-prem `ip4`/`ip6` or include entries, ending in `-all`; then set up DKIM and DMARC.

modules.title: Configure client connectivity to Microsoft 365
modules.learnSummary: This module examines how clients connect to Microsoft 365. It also provides instruction on how to configure name resolution and Outlook clients, and how to troubleshoot client connectivity.
modules.tldr: Outlook configures itself for Exchange Online through Autodiscover, which depends on the right public DNS records. Outlook connects to Exchange Online only over MAPI over HTTP. In hybrid deployments Outlook always goes through the on-prem Exchange Autodiscover first. Connectivity problems are diagnosed with Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer from the internet and the Get Help app on the client.
objectives: Describe how Outlook uses Autodiscover to connect an Outlook client to Exchange Online.
Identify the DNS records needed for Outlook and other Office-related clients to automatically locate the services in Microsoft 365 using the Autodiscover process.
Describe the connectivity protocols that enable Outlook to connect to Microsoft 365.
Identify the tools that can help you troubleshoot connectivity issues in Microsoft 365 deployments.
keyPoints: **Autodiscover** lets Outlook configure itself from just the email address and password: it finds the service via DNS, authenticates and downloads an **XML** configuration.
Required record: **CNAME** `autodiscover` → `autodiscover.outlook.com`; an extra CNAME (e.g. `autodiscover.service.<domain>`) is needed for **Exchange hybrid**.
With **split-brain DNS**, both internal and internet DNS servers must resolve the Autodiscover records.
**MAPI over HTTP** is the only protocol for Outlook to Exchange Online and Exchange Server 2019, and the only one supported by hybrid modern authentication; it's on by default.
In **hybrid**, Outlook always contacts the on-prem Exchange Autodiscover first (internally via the **Service Connection Point** in AD DS); Exchange redirects cloud mailboxes to Exchange Online.
Firewalls and proxies must allow the Microsoft 365 **endpoints** (FQDNs, ports, URLs, IPv4/IPv6 ranges).
**Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer** tests from the internet; the **Get Help** app (and `GetHelpCmd.exe` for enterprises) diagnoses and fixes problems on the device.

units.title: Examine how automatic client configuration works
points: User enters email address and password; Outlook uses the Autodiscover record in internet DNS to locate the Microsoft 365 Autodiscover service.
The client authenticates with its SMTP address and password and requests connection settings.
Microsoft 365 returns the settings as XML; Outlook applies them and connects to Exchange Online.

units.title: Explore the DNS records required for client configuration
points: Different internal namespace (`adatum.local`): internal DNS forwards queries to internet DNS. Split-brain DNS: configure Autodiscover in both.
CNAME `Autodiscover` → `autodiscover.outlook.com` for Exchange Online; CNAME for Exchange federation (e.g. `Autodiscover.service.adatum.com`) is optional but required for hybrid.
The Microsoft 365 portal lists the required records; for some providers (e.g. GoDaddy) it can create them automatically.

units.title: Configure Outlook clients
points: Protocol history: RPC/TCP → RPC/HTTP → **MAPI/HTTP**, which puts MAPI commands directly in HTTPS.

Benefits: lower latency, better handling of unstable connections, OAuth/modern auth, scalability, firewall friendliness, easier troubleshooting, faster reconnects after hibernation or network changes.
Cloud-only: Outlook uses Autodiscover records in internal or internet DNS. Hybrid: Outlook always uses the on-prem Exchange Autodiscover, which redirects cloud mailboxes via an alternate SMTP domain.
Network devices must allow Microsoft 365 endpoints: FQDNs, ports, URLs and IPv4/IPv6 ranges.

units.title: Troubleshoot client connectivity
points: **Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer**: web tool that simulates client logon and mail flow for Microsoft 365, Teams and Exchange Server, with a log and fix suggestions.

**Get Help** (built into Windows 10 and later) runs automated diagnostics and fixes for Microsoft 365 apps (install, activation, sign-in) and classic Outlook (won't start, password prompts, disconnected).
Get Help supports **classic Outlook only**, not new Outlook for Windows or new Teams.
`GetHelpCmd.exe` runs the same scenarios remotely or at scale, e.g. via PowerShell or Intune.

keyTerms.definition: Service that returns Outlook's connection settings as XML based on the user's email address.
Current Outlook transport protocol and the only one supported for Exchange Online.
AD DS object domain-joined Outlook clients use internally to locate the on-prem Exchange Autodiscover service.
FQDNs, ports, URLs and IP ranges clients use to reach Microsoft 365 services.
Web tool that tests Exchange, Teams and Microsoft 365 connectivity and mail flow from the internet.
Windows troubleshooter for Microsoft 365 apps and classic Outlook; the successor to SARA.

tables.title: Troubleshooting tools
rows: Client logon and mail flow tests for Exchange, Teams and Microsoft 365
Automated diagnostics and fixes for Microsoft 365 apps and classic Outlook
Same Get Help scenarios remotely or across many devices

remember: Outlook to Exchange Online protocol → **MAPI/HTTP**, not RPC/TCP or Outlook Anywhere (RPC/HTTP).
Hybrid Exchange → Outlook always starts at the **on-prem Autodiscover**, even for cloud mailboxes.
Test from outside the network → **Remote Connectivity Analyzer**; fix on the client → **Get Help**.

selfCheck.q: New Outlook profiles can't find Exchange Online automatically. Which DNS record do you check first?
selfCheck.a: The CNAME `autodiscover.<domain>` pointing to `autodiscover.outlook.com` in public DNS (and internal DNS too with split-brain DNS).

selfCheck.q: In a hybrid deployment, how does an internal Outlook client find a mailbox that was moved to Exchange Online?
selfCheck.a: It finds the on-prem Exchange server through the Autodiscover SCP in AD DS; Exchange returns an alternate SMTP domain that Outlook uses to reach the Microsoft 365 Autodiscover service.

selfCheck.q: Classic Outlook keeps prompting a user for their password. What built-in tool can diagnose and fix it on the device?
selfCheck.a: The Get Help app in Windows, which runs the classic Outlook troubleshooters and applies fixes automatically.

paths.title: MS-102 Manage your Microsoft 365 tenant
paths.summary: This learning path provides instruction on how to manage your Microsoft 365 tenant, including administrative roles, tenant health and services, Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise, and workplace analytics using Microsoft Viva Insights.

modules.title: Manage permissions, roles, and role groups in Microsoft 365
modules.learnSummary: This module examines the use of roles and role groups in the Microsoft 365 permission model, including role management, best practices when configuring admin roles, delegating roles, and elevating privileges.
modules.tldr: Microsoft 365 permissions come from roles (sets of permissions), scopes (where they apply) and assignments (who gets them). Roles live in several places: Microsoft Entra roles are tenant-wide, while Exchange, Intune, Defender and Purview have their own workload roles. Apply least privilege with role groups, administrative units and just-in-time access through Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management, and use SharePoint controls to stop oversharing.
objectives: Understand how roles are used in the Microsoft 365 ecosystem.
Describe the Azure role-based access control permission model used in Microsoft 365.
Identify the key tasks assigned to the common Microsoft 365 admin roles.
Identify best practices when configuring admin roles.
Delegate admin roles to partners.
Implement role groups in Microsoft 365.
Manage permissions using administrative units in Microsoft Entra ID.
Manage permissions in SharePoint to prevent oversharing of data.
Elevate privileges to access admin centers by using Microsoft Entra ID Privileged Identity Management.
keyPoints: Permission model = **roles** + **scopes** + **assignments**; assign the **least permissive role** (e.g. Password or Helpdesk Administrator to reset passwords, not Global Administrator).
Keep **two to four Global Administrators** (fewer than five), all with **MFA**, plus two **break-glass** emergency accounts; a Global Administrator can't remove their own role.
Microsoft Entra roles go to users and role-assignable groups, **Exchange roles** to users and mail-enabled groups, **Intune roles** to security groups.
**Role groups** are role-assignable groups (`isAssignableToRole` = true, set only at creation): **Assigned** membership only, no nesting, max 500 per tenant, need **Microsoft Entra ID P1**.
**Administrative units** scope a role to a subset of users, groups or devices (e.g. one region); they can't be nested and scoped admins can't create or delete users.
**PIM** makes admins **eligible** instead of permanently active: they activate a role for a limited time, with MFA, justification and optional approval; it needs **Microsoft Entra ID P2**.
Partners get delegated administration with only two roles: **Full Administration** or **Limited Administration**.
Copilot and SharePoint surface everything a user can **View**; fight oversharing by hiding "Everyone Except External Users", using data access governance reports and **Restricted Access Control**.

units.title: Examine the use of roles in the Microsoft 365 permission model
points: Roles are built-in (over 30, e.g. Exchange Administrator, Security Reader) or custom.
Scopes limit a role: directory scopes (group, site, attribute) or management scopes (service or condition).
Assignments are direct (user or group) or indirect (via membership or rule; only for custom roles and management scopes).
Role types: global, service-specific, feature-specific; categories: administrator, reader and application roles.

units.title: Manage roles across the Microsoft 365 ecosystem
points: The Microsoft 365 admin center manages Microsoft Entra roles plus Exchange and Intune roles; Microsoft Entra ID, Defender XDR and Purview also have their own workload roles in their portals.
Exchange role groups are created in the Exchange admin center and can't be assigned from the Microsoft 365 admin center (Exchange roles can).

The Exchange Administrator role from the Microsoft 365 admin center doesn't cover every Exchange admin center task; Security Administrator doesn't grant every Defender portal permission — use service-specific or Defender RBAC roles.
Defender portal: incidents, advanced hunting (KQL), threat analytics. Purview portal: compliance policies, DLP, sensitivity labels, eDiscovery, reporting.

units.title: Explore administrator roles in Microsoft 365
points: Guidelines: two to four Global Administrators, least permissive role, MFA for admins.
Only Global Administrators can reset other Global Administrators' passwords, add and manage domains and unblock another Global Administrator.
Global Reader is the read-only counterpart of Global Administrator; Helpdesk Administrator resets passwords and invalidates refresh tokens for non-admins and a few low roles.

License Administrator manages license assignments and usage location but can't buy subscriptions; Service Support Administrator handles service requests and health; Reports Reader sees usage reports and sign-in/audit logs.
Exchange Administrators should also get Service Support Administrator to see service health and message center info.

units.title: Examine best practices when configuring administrative roles
points: Least privilege = specific permissions over a specific scope for a specific time; find roles in Microsoft Entra admin center > **Roles & admins**.
Use PIM for just-in-time access; enforce MFA via PIM role settings or Conditional Access; run recurring **access reviews**.
Fewer than five Global Administrators, plus two permanent break-glass accounts that don't use the same MFA method as normal admin accounts.
Assign roles to groups and delegate per role through group owners; use **cloud-only accounts** for Microsoft Entra roles, not synced on-prem accounts.

units.title: Assign admin roles to users in Microsoft 365
points: Global Administrator includes all service admin roles; roles can be combined on one user.
Admin center: Active users > user > Roles > Edit: User (no admin access), Global administrator or a selection of admin roles; set an alternative email address for notifications.
PowerShell needs the user's object ID and the role's object ID; `Get-MgDirectoryRole` lists only **activated** roles.
Activate a role from its template with `New-MgDirectoryRole -RoleTemplateId`, then assign with `New-MgDirectoryRoleMemberByRef`.

units.title: Delegate admin roles to partners
points: A partner requests delegated administration by email; the customer accepts via the authorization link (Delegated administration > Yes).

Partners can assign only **Full Administration** (broad rights, including subscriptions, domains and security) or **Limited Administration** (users, password resets, group membership, support tickets; no domains, subscriptions or security settings).
Best practices: role matrix, document and audit roles, keep them current, get management approval.

units.title: Implement role groups in Microsoft 365
points: Assign a role to a group (e.g. Helpdesk Administrators) so membership grants the role; governance and auditing then cover the group.

Microsoft 365 admin center: security group with the roles-can-be-assigned option, or a **Private** Microsoft 365 group with "Allow admin roles to be assigned"; then assign roles and members. Microsoft Entra admin center: set the option to Yes and assign roles during creation.
PowerShell: `New-MgGroup -IsAssignableToRole:$true`, then `New-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignment`; managing membership needs `RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory`.

Protections: only Global and Privileged Role Administrators create them; no dynamic membership; no nesting; only Privileged Authentication or Global Administrators can reset members' credentials or MFA.
Make the group **eligible** through PIM (with approval) to avoid standing access.

units.title: Manage permissions using administrative units in Microsoft Entra ID
points: Container of users, groups or devices that restricts a role's scope (e.g. each university school or region); a user can be in several units.
Licensing: Microsoft Entra ID P1 per administrative unit admin, Free for members (P1 per member with dynamic membership rules).
Adding a group brings only the group into scope, not its members; scoped admins can still browse users outside the unit with default permissions.
Constraints: no nesting, scoped user admins can't create or delete users, not included in Microsoft Entra ID Governance.

units.title: Manage SharePoint permissions to prevent oversharing of data
points: Step 1: review site sharing controls, hide **Everyone Except External Users** in the People Picker, send access requests to site owners, default to specific-people links.
Step 2: find inactive sites (Inactive Site Policies), then restrict or delete them.
Step 3: **data access governance reports** (SharePoint Advanced Management) show 28-day use of Everyone Except External Users, org-wide links and Anyone links.
Steps 4–5: remediate with **Restricted Access Control**, Change History, Site Access Review by owners, and block download policies on business-critical sites.

units.title: Elevate privileges using Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management
points: PIM gives just-in-time access to Microsoft Entra roles, Microsoft 365, Intune and Azure resources, with activation history, alerts, approvals and membership reviews.
**Eligible** admins have an inactive role until they complete activation for a predetermined time — no standing admin access.
The **Privileged Role Administrator** manages PIM, approves requests and sets durations.
Activate via Microsoft Entra admin center > Privileged Identity Management > **My roles** > Eligible assignments > Activate: MFA, optional reduced scope and start time, reason; approval if required.
Applications that cached roles may not reflect activation or deactivation immediately; signing out and in can help.

keyTerms.definition: Granting only the permissions needed, over the smallest scope, for the shortest time.
Group with `isAssignableToRole` = true that passes Microsoft Entra roles to its members.
Microsoft Entra container of users, groups or devices used to scope admin roles.
Microsoft Entra service for just-in-time, time-bound, approvable role activation.
A role a user may activate when needed instead of holding it permanently.
Permanent emergency Global Administrator account kept for lockout scenarios.
SharePoint Advanced Management policy that limits a site's access to a specified group.

tables.title: Common admin roles
rows: Everything; only role that can reset other Global Administrators, manage domains, unblock Global Administrators
Read-only view of all admin settings; no Purchase services
Users, groups, licenses, password resets for non-admins and low roles
Password resets, force sign-out, service requests, service health
License assignments and usage location; can't buy subscriptions
All groups and group creation, expiration and naming policies
Service requests, message center, service health
Security policies and alerts / eDiscovery, data governance, compliance alerts

tables.title: Licensing for delegation features
rows: P1 per unit admin; Free per member (P1 per member with dynamic rules)

remember: Someone only needs to reset passwords → **Helpdesk or Password Administrator**, not Global Administrator.
Regional admins should manage only their region's users → **administrative units**, not separate tenants or custom groups.
Admin access only when needed, with approval → **PIM eligible assignment** (P2), not a permanent role.
Role groups can't be **dynamic** or **nested**, and an existing group can't be converted into one.

selfCheck.q: An admin gave Global Administrator to a user who only manages Office cloud policies and self-service downloads. Which guideline is broken?
selfCheck.a: Assign the least permissive role; Office Apps Administrator would cover those tasks.

selfCheck.q: Helpdesk staff in London should reset passwords only for London users. What do you configure?
selfCheck.a: An administrative unit containing the London users, with the Helpdesk Administrator role assigned scoped to that unit.

selfCheck.q: You want to assign the Helpdesk Administrator role to an existing security group. Why does this fail?
selfCheck.a: Only groups created with `isAssignableToRole` set to true can hold roles, and the property can't be changed afterwards; create a new role-assignable group.

modules.title: Manage tenant health and services in Microsoft 365
modules.learnSummary: This module examines how to monitor your organization's transition to Microsoft 365 using Microsoft 365 tools. It also examines how to develop an incident response plan and request assistance from Microsoft.
modules.tldr: Monitor tenant health in the Microsoft 365 admin center with Service health, Adoption Score, usage analytics and network connectivity insights. Microsoft 365 Backup adds fast, pay-as-you-go backup and restore for SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange. When something breaks, follow an incident response plan and open a service request with Microsoft Support.
objectives: Monitor your organization's Microsoft 365 service health in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Implement Microsoft 365 network connectivity for assessments and insights.
Implement Microsoft 365 Backup (Preview) for fast content backup and restoration.
Develop an incident response plan to deal with incidents that can occur with your Microsoft 365 service.
Request assistance from Microsoft to address technical, presales, billing, and subscription support issues.
keyPoints: **Health > Service health** shows incidents and advisories per service; **Service restored** means the fix is complete. Email notifications go to up to **two addresses** per admin.

**Adoption Score** measures 8 categories (5 people experiences, 3 technology experiences), max **800 points**, based on organization-level data from the last **28 days**; turn it on as Global Administrator.
**Usage analytics** in Power BI needs a **Power BI Pro** license and shows 12 months of data; user names are **hidden by default** in reports since September 2021.
**Network connectivity** (Health > Network connectivity) needs office locations: Windows Location Services, manually added **IPv4** LAN subnets, or the network connectivity test.
Network insights flag issues like **backhauled egress** (>500 miles), intermediary devices (proxy, VPN) and non-optimal service front doors — aim for **local, direct egress**.
**Microsoft 365 Backup** costs **$0.15/GB/month**, keeps immutable backups for 365 days inside the Microsoft 365 trust boundary, and restores 1,000 units in under 12 hours.
Incident plan: **validate** the incident → check **relevance** → check the **timeline** → prepare a **backup solution**.
Support severity: **A** critical (service down, many users), **B** high (impaired, moderate impact), **C** noncritical (workaround exists).

units.title: Monitor the health of your Microsoft 365 services
points: The Health dashboard shows critical alerts (incidents, billing problems), service health and usage, license use and recommended actions (MFA for admins, monthly Office updates, OneDrive training).

Statuses run from Investigating, Service degradation and Service interruption through Restoring service and Extended recovery to **Service restored**, False positive or Post-incident report published.
Service health tabs: Overview, Issue history (all or last 7 days), Reported issues; use **Report an issue** for problems not listed and **Customize** to choose services.
Email notifications: Customize > Email, up to two addresses per admin, for incidents or advisories per service, or per individual issue.

units.title: Monitor tenant health using Microsoft 365 Adoption Score
points: People experiences: communication, meetings, content collaboration, teamwork, mobility. Technology experiences: endpoint analytics, network connectivity, Microsoft 365 Apps health.
Turn on in Reports > **Adoption Score** (Global Administrator); insights take up to 24 hours. Endpoint analytics needs Intune; no Viva Insights license is required.
Each category is worth 100 points (max 800), updated daily over the last 28 days; peer benchmarks compare with similar organizations. Network connectivity benchmark: 80 points.
Insights are organization-level, not individual; group-level aggregates and **organizational messages** help drive adoption.

units.title: Monitor tenant health using Microsoft 365 usage analytics
points: Admin center Activity reports cover 7/30/90/180 days; the Power BI template app shows monthly data for up to 12 months and can be sliced by AD attributes like department.
Enable in Reports > Usage > Microsoft 365 usage analytics > Get started (Global Administrator); data collection takes up to 48 hours. Connect the app with the tenant ID and **OAuth2**.
Reports: Executive Summary, Microsoft 365 Overview (adoption, usage, communication, collaboration, storage, mobility), Activation and Licensing, Product usage, User activity.
User-level detail arrives around the fifth of the next month; Global Reader and Usage Summary Reports Reader can't see user activity reports.
To show real names: Settings > Org settings > Reports > clear **Display concealed user, group, and site names in all reports** (logged in the audit log).

units.title: Implement Microsoft 365 Network Connectivity Assessments and Insights
points: Option 1: Windows Location Services (off by default; at least two Wi-Fi computers per office with current OneDrive; city-level). Option 2: add locations with LAN subnets (IPv4 only; multiple offices per city). Option 3: run the **network connectivity test** at each office.
Assessments score 0–100 per location and tenant-wide; most useful for enterprises with over 500 users and multiple offices.
Reports Reader can view; **Service Support Administrator** is needed to configure locations.
Insights: backhauled egress, network intermediary device, better performance for nearby customers, non-optimal Exchange/SharePoint front door, low SharePoint download speed (<1 MBps), China egress.

units.title: Implement Microsoft 365 Backup (Preview)
points: Pay-as-you-go service for SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts and Exchange mailboxes, in the admin center or via partner apps on the Microsoft 365 Backup Storage platform.
Billed on protected content size including recycle bins; restore points and restores are free; deleted content is still billed for its 365-day retention.
Backups are immutable and stay within the Microsoft 365 trust boundary and data residency geography.
A new policy takes about 60 minutes to process plus 60 minutes for restore points; in-place restores with a "faster" restore point are quickest.

units.title: Develop an incident response plan
points: Microsoft 365 is a managed evergreen service; a service can be degraded in one tenant region and healthy in another.
Steps: validate the incident affects you, determine relevance with specialist admins, check the expected timeline (or open a service request with the incident number), prepare a fallback.
Always check Service health for updates; service requests are free with the subscription.

units.title: Request assistance from Microsoft
points: Support covers technical, presales, billing and subscription issues, online and by phone, for paid and trial subscriptions.
Only users with admin roles can contact Microsoft about service requests.

Admin's job: account setup, client connectivity and software issues, availability within the organization's control, self-service resources. Microsoft's job: troubleshooting, coordination, licensing and billing help.
Submit via Support > **New service request**; Microsoft assigns severity A, B or C.

keyTerms.definition: Admin center page listing incidents and advisories for each Microsoft 365 service in your tenant.
Organization-level score (max 800) for people and technology experiences, with peer benchmarks.
Power BI template app with 12 months of Microsoft 365 usage data.
Where office traffic leaves to the internet; should be local and close to users.
A OneDrive account, SharePoint site or Exchange mailbox protected by Microsoft 365 Backup.
Microsoft Support case levels: critical, high, noncritical.

tables.title: Ways to provide office locations for network connectivity
rows: Opt-in setting; at least two Wi-Fi computers per office with current OneDrive; location consent
Locations found automatically at city level; one office per city
LAN subnets (IPv4) per office; current OneDrive on at least one computer
Someone at each office runs the test as local admin

remember: Steps to resolve the incident are complete → **Service restored**, not Restoring service or Extended recovery.
Configure network connectivity locations → **Service Support Administrator**; Reports Reader can only view.
Usage analytics in Power BI → **Power BI Pro** license; Adoption Score → no Viva Insights license needed.
When opening a service request, the admin handles **client connectivity and software issues**; Microsoft troubleshoots and coordinates.

selfCheck.q: Users complain Exchange Online is slow. What should you check before calling support?
selfCheck.a: Service health in the Microsoft 365 admin center, to see whether there's a known incident or advisory with a resolution in progress.

selfCheck.q: Network insights show traffic from your Brussels office leaves the internet in Frankfurt through a central proxy. What's the recommendation?
selfCheck.a: Use local, direct network egress close to the office and let Microsoft 365 traffic bypass intermediary devices such as proxies.

selfCheck.q: Ransomware encrypted a SharePoint site protected by Microsoft 365 Backup. How do you restore it fastest?
selfCheck.a: Do an in-place restore of the whole site using one of the recommended "faster" restore points.

modules.title: Deploy Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise
modules.learnSummary: This module examines how to implement the Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise productivity suite in both user-driven and centralized deployments.
modules.tldr: Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise is the locally installed Office suite, delivered with Click-to-Run. Users can install it themselves from the portal, or admins can deploy it centrally with Configuration Manager, the Office Deployment Tool (from the Office CDN or a local share) or Intune. Updates follow an update channel (Current, Monthly Enterprise, Semi-Annual Enterprise). The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center and the Intune security baseline handle ongoing management and security.
objectives: Describe the Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise functionality.
Plan a deployment strategy for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise.
Complete a user-driven installation of Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise.
Deploy Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise with Microsoft Configuration Manager.
Identify the mechanisms for managing centralized deployments of Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise.
Deploy Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise with the Office Deployment Toolkit.
Describe how to manage Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise updates.
Determine which update channel and application method applies for your organization.
Add Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise to Microsoft Intune.
Deploy Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise security baseline.
keyPoints: The apps **install and run locally** via **Click-to-Run** streaming; users must connect to the internet at least **every 30 days** to validate the license. Visio and Project aren't included.
**Self-service** install from the portal needs local **admin rights** and gives little control; block it in Org settings > **Microsoft 365 installation options**.
The **Office Deployment Tool** (`setup.exe`) uses a `configuration.xml` built with the **Office Customization Tool**: `/download` to a local share, `/configure` to install.
Best practice: two packages and groups — **pilot** on Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel (Preview), **broad** on Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel; remove previous **MSI** versions.

Update channels: **Current** (newest features as soon as ready, recommended), **Monthly Enterprise** (once a month, second Tuesday), **Semi-Annual Enterprise** (features in January and July, for devices needing extensive testing).
Updates download only the **deltas**; clients on an outdated build are supported for only **12 months**.
In **Intune**, the Microsoft 365 Apps (Windows 10 and later) app type installs the suite; select **Remove MSI** or installation fails. For Autopilot ESP, deploy it as a **Win32** app.
The **Microsoft 365 Apps admin center** offers the Office cloud policy service, Office Customization Tool, Apps health, inventory, security update status and **servicing profiles**.

units.title: Explore Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise functionality
points: Formerly Office 365 ProPlus; includes Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Access, Publisher, OneNote and Teams (no Access or Publisher on Mac).
Click-to-Run streaming: users can start an app while installation continues in the background; it isn't a web or light version.
Internet connection needed at least every 30 days for license validation.
Visio and Project are separate subscriptions, downloadable the same way once enabled in the admin center.

units.title: Complete a self-service installation of Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise
points: Always streams from the internet (no local source), needs a licensed account and local admin rights; updates install automatically from the internet.
Obstacles: lack of IT expertise, bandwidth (packages of several GB downloaded at the same time) and users without local admin rights.
Block all self-service installs: Settings > Org settings > Services > Microsoft 365 installation options > Installation tab > clear **Office (includes Skype for Business)**.

units.title: Deploy Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise with Microsoft Configuration Manager
points: Recommended for existing Configuration Manager customers (current branch): scales, offers the Office Client Management dashboard, Office Customization Tool integration, removal of old Office and **peer cache** for remote sites.
Requirements: client internet access for activation; the console needs HTTPS 443 access to `config.office.com`.
Create apps with **Office 365 Installer** in Software Library > Office 365 Client Management; deploy to a pilot collection, then the broad collection.
Configuration Manager doesn't manage Office updates by default; check results in the Office 365 Client Management dashboard (may need hardware inventory).

units.title: Deploy Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise from the cloud
points: The ODT is a command-line tool that downloads, installs or removes Click-to-Run Office and applies update settings.

Build `config-pilot-SECP.xml` and `config-broad-SEC.xml` in the Office Customization Tool: products, channel, languages (Match operating system, Fallback to the CDN), installation from the **Office CDN**, automatic updates, remove MSI, silent install with EULA accepted.
Deploy with `setup.exe /configure <config.xml>` from an elevated prompt or script; troubleshoot with the latest ODT, correct paths and the log in `%temp%`.
The unit also explains Office 365 CDN origins: public (anonymous, for JS, CSS, nonsensitive images) and private (token-secured SharePoint content).

units.title: Deploy Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise from a local source
points: Eight steps instead of five: create shares (`M365`, `M365\SECP`, `M365\SEC`) with Read permission, download the ODT, build configs with **Local source** paths, run `setup.exe /download`, then `/configure`.
Downloading into a folder that already has that version fetches only missing files (e.g. an extra language).
Use multiple shares (e.g. DFS in branch offices) to improve availability and save bandwidth.

units.title: Manage updates to Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise
points: A full build is released monthly on Patch Tuesday; clients download only the differences and switch to the new build when the app restarts.
Options: **automatic from cloud** (default), **automatic from network** (internal source via Group Policy or configuration.xml) or **rerun setup.exe via ESD** such as Configuration Manager.
Test new builds on a pilot share before moving them to production; builds older than 12 months aren't supported.
configuration.xml `<Updates Enabled="TRUE" UpdatePath="\\Server\Share\" TargetVersion="..."/>` controls update source and version.

units.title: Explore the update channels for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise
points: Current Channel: features at least monthly, no fixed schedule; Current Channel (Preview) releases a week or more earlier for a test group.
Monthly Enterprise Channel: one predictable update on the second Tuesday; no preview channel.
Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel: features in January and July; its Preview channel gets them in March and September, four months earlier.
Set the channel in the admin center (Office installation options), the ODT configuration.xml or Group Policy (Office administrative templates).

units.title: Manage your cloud apps using the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center
points: Open via All admin centers > **Office configuration**.
**Office cloud policy service** enforces Office policies per user, even on non-domain-joined devices, and some settings for Office for the web.
Apps health (crash rate, boot time), Inventory (devices, builds, add-ins, macros), Security update status with a self-set goal.
**Servicing profiles** move devices to Monthly Enterprise Channel with updates from the CDN in waves, with pause, deadlines and exclusion dates.

units.title: Add Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise to Microsoft Intune
points: Intune app types: store, line-of-business, built-in, web link, and apps from other Microsoft services; add them in **Apps > All apps > Add**.
Microsoft 365 Apps (Windows 10 and later): configure architecture, default file format, update channel, languages and **Remove MSI**, then assign to groups.
Only one Microsoft 365 Apps deployment per device; a later assignment **overwrites** earlier ones (an app left out gets uninstalled, except Visio and Project).
Not supported on Windows Home, Team or Holographic; 64-bit installs only on 64-bit devices; don't mix with Store (Centennial) Office apps.
During Autopilot ESP, deploy Microsoft 365 Apps as a Win32 app to avoid install conflicts with the Intune Management Extension.

units.title: Deploy Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise security baseline
points: Security baselines are Microsoft-recommended setting groups; available for Windows, Defender for Endpoint, Edge, Windows 365 and Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise.
Create in Intune admin center > Endpoint security > **Security baselines** > Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise Security Baseline > Create profile.
Assign the profile to device groups or user groups, with optional exclusions; review settings and scope tags in the wizard.
Benefits: stronger security, compliance, central management and a consistent user experience.

Users offline for weeks → they must connect **every 30 days**, not stay permanently online.

selfCheck.q: You want to stop all users from installing Microsoft 365 Apps themselves from the portal. Where do you do this?
selfCheck.a: In Settings > Org settings > Microsoft 365 installation options > Installation, clear the Office (includes Skype for Business) check box.

selfCheck.q: A regulated department can only accept new Office features twice a year after testing. Which channel do you use, and for whom is the preview?
selfCheck.a: Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel for the broad group, with a small pilot group on Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel (Preview).

selfCheck.q: Your branch office has slow internet. How do you install Microsoft 365 Apps there with the ODT?
selfCheck.a: Run `setup.exe /download` to a local share (configured as Local source in the config file), then have clients run `setup.exe /configure` from that share.

modules.title: Analyze your Microsoft 365 workplace data using Microsoft Viva Insights
modules.learnSummary: This module examines the workplace analytical features of Microsoft Viva Insights, including how it works, and how it generates insights and improves collaboration within an organization.
modules.tldr: Viva Insights turns Microsoft 365 collaboration metadata, combined with HR organizational data, into privacy-protected insights about productivity and wellbeing. It works at four levels: Personal insights (only you), Team insights (managers with direct reports), Organization insights (leaders) and Advanced insights (analysts with queries and Power BI templates). Viva Insights roles decide who sees and configures what.
objectives: Identify how Microsoft Viva Insights can help improve collaboration behaviors in your organization.
Describe how the Personal insights app analyzes how you work.
Describe how the Team insights app provides visibility into team work habits that might lead to stress and burnout.
Describe how the Organization insights app enables managers to see how their work culture affects employee wellbeing.
Describe how the Advanced insights app addresses critical questions about resiliency and work culture.
keyPoints: Four levels: **Personal** (only you see it), **Team** (managers with direct reports), **Organization** (business leaders and group managers) and **Advanced** (analysts: queries and Power BI templates).
Viva Insights processes only **metadata** (who, when, subject, attendance), refreshed **weekly**, joined with **organizational (HR) data**; results are de-identified and aggregated.
Privacy principle: no user can learn anything about an identified person they **couldn't already know**; personal insights live in the user's own **mailbox** and managers can't see them.
The **Insights Administrator** uploads organizational data and sets privacy settings but isn't a Microsoft 365 admin and can't see Microsoft 365 data unless given such a role.
**Team insights** require at least **one direct report** in Microsoft Entra ID or the uploaded HR file; team membership can't be edited.

**Organization insights** need a Viva Insights (premium) license for viewer and measured employees, the **Insights Business Leader** role or group-manager status, and a group above the **minimum group size**.
Organizational data comes from **Microsoft Entra ID** (default) or a UTF-8 **.csv** upload with required attributes plus up to **100 optional** ones.

units.title: Examine the analytical features of Microsoft Viva Insights
points: Part of Microsoft Viva; available as a Teams and web app plus Outlook features.
Collaboration metadata (email, meetings, Teams chats and calls) is combined with uploaded HR attributes, then de-identified into behavioral metrics.

Roles: Insights Administrator (data upload, privacy settings), Insights Business Leader (My organization), People Manager (My team), Analyst (full analysis incl. Query designer), Analyst (Limited Access) (no Query designer), Program Manager (plans in Advanced insights).
Updating organizational data monthly or quarterly keeps analysis accurate.

units.title: Explore Personal insights
points: Helps users strengthen relationships, protect focus time and improve work-life balance (breaks, Headspace meditation, virtual commute).
Delivered via the Viva Insights app in Teams and on the web, the Outlook add-in, **briefing emails**, digest emails and inline suggestions in Outlook.
Uses data already in the user's Exchange Online mailbox: email metadata, calendar items, Teams calls and chats, OneDrive/SharePoint document counts.
Data is stored in the mailbox with the same protection as email; only the user sees it and no tracking software runs on the PC.

units.title: Explore Team insights
points: For managers with direct reports; shows team habits that lead to stress and burnout, without individual members' personal data.
Teams are built from Microsoft Entra ID (default) or an uploaded HR file; keep it updated, changes show in the next week's data.
Users opt in or out under Settings > Team insights; pin the Viva Insights app in Teams after an admin installs it.
Managers who multitask in meetings are more than twice as likely to have team members who do; shared no-meeting day, focus and meeting plans help set norms.

units.title: Explore Organization insights
points: Shows leaders indicators of wellbeing, productivity and team culture for direct and indirect reports (group managers) or the whole company (Insights Business Leader).
