Measured employees must have a Viva Insights license, be in the hierarchy and have been active in Outlook or Teams that week.
Cards offer scope selector, indicators, Show details, Share (Teams chat or link) and **Set up plan** (e.g. no-meeting day).
Tabs: Home, Wellbeing, Productivity, Teamwork; metrics include uninterrupted focus hours, after-hours collaboration, meeting hours, multitasking hours, join on time rate, internal network size.

units.title: Explore Advanced insights
points: Analysis tools for analysts (Insights Analyst role) on resiliency, wellbeing and hybrid work.
Organizational data: identify trends, choose attributes (job role, region, manager…), export from HR, structure as UTF-8 .csv with an alphanumeric file name, then upload.
Power BI templates: Business resilience, Hybrid workforce experience, Manager effectiveness, Meeting effectiveness, Ways of working, Wellbeing.
**Custom person queries** return one row per person per period; **custom meeting queries** analyze meeting types, attendees and effectiveness.

keyTerms.definition: Descriptive HR attributes about employees, from Microsoft Entra ID or an uploaded .csv, used to group and filter insights.
Email, meeting, chat and call details such as time, participants and subject — not content — used by Viva Insights.
Viva Insights role that uploads organizational data and configures privacy and system settings.
Role that sees Organization insights for all measured employees in the tenant.
A licensed, active employee included in Organization insights.
Admin-set threshold below which group-level insights aren't shown, to protect privacy.

tables.title: Viva Insights levels
rows: Own work habits, focus time, breaks, relationships
Managers with at least one direct report
Team habits that lead to burnout and stress
Insights Business Leaders and group managers
Work culture effects on wellbeing and productivity
Custom queries, Power BI templates, plans

remember: Can't see Team insights despite the People Manager role → you have **no direct reports**.
Process changes to improve business outcomes and protect wellbeing → **Advanced insights**; wellbeing view of your own org → **Organization insights**.
Insights Administrator ≠ Microsoft 365 admin — it has access to **organizational data only**.
Personal insights are **private**: managers and admins can't view them.

selfCheck.q: An HR analyst with no direct reports was given the People Manager role but can't access Team insights. Why?
selfCheck.a: Team insights are built from direct reports in Microsoft Entra ID or the HR file; without at least one direct report there's no team to show.

selfCheck.q: A director wants Organization insights for the whole company. What's required?
selfCheck.a: A Viva Insights license, the Insights Business Leader role, and licensed, active measured employees meeting the minimum group size.

selfCheck.q: Who uploads the HR file used for Viva Insights, and in what format?
selfCheck.a: The Insights Administrator uploads a UTF-8 encoded .csv with the required attributes (plus up to 100 optional ones) in the Advanced insights app.

paths.title: MS-102 Implement identity synchronization
paths.summary: This learning path examines how organizations should plan for and implement identity synchronization in a hybrid Microsoft 365 deployment. You learn how to implement Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync, and how to manage synchronized identities.

modules.title: Explore identity synchronization
modules.learnSummary: This module examines identity synchronization using Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and explores the authentication and provisioning options that can be used and the inner-workings of directory synchronization.
modules.tldr: Microsoft 365 uses Microsoft Entra ID for identity, either as cloud-only accounts or as hybrid identities synchronized from on-premises AD DS. Hybrid identities authenticate through managed authentication (password hash synchronization or pass-through authentication) or federation (such as AD FS). Microsoft recommends enabling password hash synchronization whatever primary method you choose.
objectives: Describe the Microsoft 365 authentication and provisioning options
Explain the two identity models in Microsoft 365 - cloud-only identity and hybrid identity
Explain the three authentication methods in the hybrid identity model - Password hash synchronization, Pass-through authentication, and federated authentication
Describe how Microsoft 365 commonly uses directory synchronization
keyPoints: **Cloud-only identity**: accounts exist only in Microsoft Entra ID. It's simple and needs no extra servers, so it suits organizations without AD DS. You manage the accounts in the Microsoft 365 admin center or PowerShell.
**Hybrid identity**: accounts originate in AD DS and a copy lives in Microsoft Entra ID. On-premises AD DS is the **authoritative source**, so you manage synchronized users with your AD DS tools.
Synced users get **no licence automatically**. Set a **usage location** first, then assign a licence directly or through group membership.

**Password hash synchronization (PHS)**: Microsoft Entra ID authenticates using a hash of the password hash. The actual password is never sent or stored, and no extra infrastructure is needed beyond the sync tool.

**Pass-through authentication (PTA)**: lightweight on-premises agents validate credentials against AD DS. Use it when account states, password policies and sign-in hours must be **enforced immediately**.

**Federated authentication**: Microsoft Entra ID hands sign-in to another identity provider, such as **AD FS** (SSO via SAML) or a compatible third party. Since Windows Server 2012 R2, **Web Application Proxy** replaces the federation server proxy.
Directory sync is mostly **one-way** (on-premises → cloud), but Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and Cloud Sync can **write back** specific objects and attributes.
**Enable PHS** with any method for high availability, survival of an on-premises outage, and **leaked credential detection** in Identity Protection.

units.title: Examine identity models for Microsoft 365
points: Cloud-only identity: accounts exist only in the Microsoft Entra tenant, which also authenticates them. Typical for small and medium-sized organizations without AD DS.
Hybrid identity: the AD DS account has a copy in Microsoft Entra ID, which may include a hash of the AD DS password hash. Users keep the same credentials on-premises and in the cloud.
Microsoft Entra groups enable group-based licensing, dynamic membership on attributes (e.g. department), SaaS provisioning, and access to Teams and SharePoint sites.
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync runs on an on-premises server, is self-maintained and scales to complex forests. It supports PHS, device registration and AD FS integration.
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync is hosted and managed by Microsoft and syncs only users, groups and contacts. It's designed for smaller, simpler AD environments.

units.title: Examine authentication options for the hybrid identity model
points: Managed authentication means Microsoft Entra ID handles sign-in, using either PHS or PTA. With federated authentication, Microsoft Entra ID redirects sign-in to another identity provider.
PHS is a secure one-way hash sync: password changes on-premises sync to the cloud. Some premium features, such as Identity Protection, require PHS.
PTA agents on one or more on-premises servers validate credentials against AD DS. No password hashes are stored in Microsoft Entra ID.

Federation suits large enterprises with complex requirements. AD FS provides SSO via SAML. Web Application Proxy (from Windows Server 2012 R2) acts as the AD FS proxy and adds support for OAuth/OpenID Connect.
Third-party identity providers (e.g. PingFederate, Okta) are supported if they're compatible with Microsoft Entra ID. Synced accounts can't be managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center or PowerShell.

units.title: Explore directory synchronization
points: Directory synchronization syncs users, groups, contacts and computers between directories. For Microsoft 365, that's usually on-premises AD → Microsoft Entra ID, and it can include HR databases or LDAP.
Writeback of specific objects and attributes, plus two-way password sync, creates a form of two-way sync. Install Microsoft Entra Connect Sync on a dedicated on-premises computer.
Benefits: common hybrid identity, SSO, MFA, Conditional Access policies, and one identity for Microsoft 365, Intune and SaaS apps.
PHS is recommended with any method. PTA and federation depend on on-premises infrastructure, and with PHS, organizations hit by ransomware were back online within hours rather than weeks.
Identity Protection (Microsoft Entra ID P2) uses PHS to detect leaked credentials and can block those users or force a password change.

keyTerms.definition: Syncs a hash of the AD DS password hash to Microsoft Entra ID, which then authenticates users itself.
On-premises software agents validate cloud sign-ins directly against AD DS; no hashes stored in the cloud.
Microsoft Entra ID redirects sign-in to a trusted identity provider such as AD FS or a compatible third party.
Active Directory Federation Services: Microsoft's SSO and identity federation service using SAML and other protocols.
Remote Access role service that replaced the federation server proxy from Windows Server 2012 R2 onward.
Synchronizing specific objects or attributes from Microsoft Entra ID back to on-premises AD.

tables.title: Hybrid authentication methods
rows: Microsoft Entra ID (using the synced hash)
Simplest; resilient to on-premises outages; enables leaked credential detection
On-premises AD DS via PTA agents
One or more servers running agents
Immediately enforce on-premises account states, password policies and sign-in hours
Federation servers plus proxies (WAP) in the perimeter network
Large enterprises with complex authentication requirements

remember: Synced user can't use Microsoft 365 → set a **usage location** and assign a **licence**; sync doesn't do this automatically.
Need cloud **leaked credential detection** or resilience to on-premises outages → enable **PHS**, even when PTA or federation is primary.
Edit a synced user's attributes → do it in **on-premises AD DS**, not in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Federation server proxy is legacy; from Windows Server 2012 R2 onward think **Web Application Proxy**.

selfCheck.q: A company must block cloud sign-in the moment an account is disabled or outside its allowed logon hours in AD DS, without deploying federation. Which method fits?
selfCheck.a: Pass-through authentication. Its agents validate every sign-in directly against on-premises AD DS.

selfCheck.q: Which identity model suits a small business that has no on-premises servers?
selfCheck.a: Cloud-only identity: accounts exist only in Microsoft Entra ID and need no extra directory tools or servers.

selfCheck.q: An organization uses AD FS. Why should it still enable password hash synchronization?
selfCheck.a: PHS is a fallback if the on-premises infrastructure fails, and it lets Identity Protection detect leaked credentials.

modules.title: Prepare for identity synchronization to Microsoft 365
modules.learnSummary: This module examines all the planning aspects that must be considered when implementing directory synchronization between on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID.
modules.tldr: Before you sync on-premises AD to Microsoft Entra ID, deploy Microsoft Entra ID in phases, clean up your directory (IdFix, UPN suffixes) and accept that on-premises AD becomes the source of authority. Then choose a sync tool. Microsoft Entra Connect Sync is a full-featured on-premises server. Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync uses lightweight agents with its configuration in the cloud.
objectives: Identify the tasks necessary to configure your Microsoft Entra ID environment.
Plan directory synchronization to synchronize your on-premises Active Directory objects to Microsoft Entra ID.
Identify the features of Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync.
Choose which directory synchronization best fits your environment and business needs.
keyPoints: Deploy Microsoft Entra ID in **four phases**: security foundation → import users, sync and devices → manage applications → audit privileged identities, access reviews and lifecycle automation.
Phase 1 starts with **two to four cloud-only emergency Global Administrators**, nonglobal admin roles, SSPR, banned passwords, blocking legacy authentication and MFA through Conditional Access.
Once an object syncs, its **source of authority** moves to on-premises AD. From then on you edit it only with **on-premises AD tools**, so treat sync as a long-term commitment.
Clean up AD first: remove duplicate **proxyAddresses/userPrincipalName**, fix blank or invalid UPNs and remove invalid characters. **IdFix** finds and fixes most sync errors.
Use a **routable UPN suffix**; Microsoft recommends UPN = **primary SMTP address**. A non-routable suffix such as `.local` falls back to the **onmicrosoft.com** domain.

**Connect Sync**: configuration and provisioning on the on-premises server. It covers more features (PTA, device and group writeback, LDAP, attribute filtering, Exchange hybrid writeback), but costs more to run and maintain.

**Cloud Sync**: lightweight agents and configuration stored in the cloud. It supports **disconnected forests** and multiple agents for high availability (only one active at a time), and syncs more often than Connect Sync's 30-minute cycle.
Connect Sync's default **SQL Server 2019 Express LocalDB** (10 GB) handles about **100,000 objects**; beyond that you need full SQL Server. Treat the sync server as a **Tier 0** asset.

units.title: Plan your Microsoft Entra ID deployment
points: The phases can run over 30, 60, 90 days or more, and many tasks need only Microsoft Entra Free.

Phase 1 (security foundation): emergency admins and least-privilege roles (Free), SSPR, custom banned passwords, smart lockout, MFA and legacy-auth blocking via Conditional Access (P1). PIM and Identity Protection need P2.

Phase 2: install Connect Sync, enable PHS (Free), password writeback, Connect Health and group-based licensing (P1). Also plan guest access, device strategy, Windows Hello for Business and passwordless sign-in.
Phase 3: identify apps, integrate gallery SaaS apps (Free) and publish on-premises apps with Application Proxy (P1).
Phase 4: enforce PIM and run access reviews (P2). Add dynamic groups, group-based app provisioning and automated provisioning from HR (P1).

units.title: Prepare for directory synchronization
points: Provisioning means creating, updating and deleting an object based on conditions, e.g. from HR to AD, Microsoft Entra ID and apps.
Prepare AD: identify the source of authority, clean up attributes and set up auditing.
If a user's Microsoft 365 UPN doesn't match on-premises (e.g. licensed before the domain was verified), fix it with PowerShell. Check app dependencies before you change UPN suffixes.

IdFix queries all domains in the forest. It edits only selected objects, supports rollback, excludes critical system objects, exports and imports CSV/LDF and logs verbosely. Use it carefully, because it bulk-updates objects.

units.title: Choose your directory synchronization tool
points: Connect Sync runs on a domain-joined server (or a DC) and needs only outbound HTTPS. Its features include filtering, PHS, password and device writeback, accidental-delete prevention (500 deletes per run by default) and automatic upgrade.
Connect Sync has two components: the synchronization services and Microsoft Entra Connect Health. Use custom settings for multiple forests or optional features.
Cloud Sync uses a lightweight agent, needs no SQL Server and is easier to set up. It's ideal for disconnected forests (e.g. mergers) and can run side by side with Connect Sync.

Only Connect Sync supports: LDAP, device objects, filtering on attribute values, PTA, device/group/Exchange hybrid writeback, Microsoft Entra Domain Services, unlimited objects per domain and groups of up to 250,000 members.
Both support: PHS, federation, Seamless SSO, password writeback, filtering on domains/OUs/groups, up to 150,000 objects per AD domain and on-demand provisioning.

units.title: Plan for directory synchronization using Microsoft Entra Connect Sync
points: Without PHS, single sign-on needs AD FS or PTA (or users keep a separate cloud password).
Tenant object limits: 50,000 by default and 300,000 after domain verification. Beyond that, open a support case; more than 500,000 objects needs a licence (e.g. Microsoft 365).

AD requirements: schema and forest level Windows Server 2003 or later, a writable DC (no RODC), no dotted NetBIOS names, and AD Recycle Bin recommended. Set the PowerShell execution policy to RemoteSigned.
External SQL Server needs a case-insensitive (`_CI_`) collation and one sync engine per instance. Azure SQL Database isn't supported.

Accounts: Global Administrator or Hybrid Identity Administrator in Microsoft Entra ID, plus Enterprise Admin for express setup. Version 2.0+ requires TLS 1.2. Set the proxy idle timeout to at least 6 minutes.

units.title: Plan for directory synchronization using Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
points: Topologies: single forest, multi-forest, an existing Connect Sync forest plus a new forest on Cloud Sync, or a pilot in a forest already synced by Connect Sync (each object in scope of only one tool).
There's no matching across forests: represent each user or group only once. The source anchor is ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid, or ObjectGUID if that's absent, and can't be changed.

Prerequisites: a gMSA to run the agent (created with Domain or Enterprise Admin), a non-guest Hybrid Identity Administrator, a Windows Server 2016+ Tier 0 server (a DC is allowed) and firewall configuration.
Microsoft recommends three active agents for high availability.

keyTerms.definition: Where an object is mastered; after sync it moves from Microsoft 365 to on-premises AD.
Tool that finds and fixes AD attribute errors (duplicates, invalid characters, bad UPNs) before sync.
The part of the UPN after the @; it should be a routable, verified domain.
On-premises sync server with configuration and provisioning stored locally and a SQL database.
Lightweight agent-based sync whose configuration is stored and provisioning run in the cloud.
Group Managed Service Account: a domain account with automatic password management, used to run the Cloud Sync agent.
Immutable attribute linking on-premises and cloud objects (ms-DS-ConsistencyGuid or ObjectGUID).

tables.title: Connect Sync vs Cloud Sync (selected differences)
rows: In the cloud (Microsoft Entra provisioning service)
LDAP directories, device objects, attribute-value filtering

remember: Disconnected forests after a merger → **Cloud Sync**; PTA, device writeback or LDAP → **Connect Sync**.
More than ~100,000 objects with Connect Sync → **full SQL Server** instead of LocalDB.
Connect Sync can't use a **read-only domain controller** and doesn't support **dotted NetBIOS names**.
Cloud Sync agents give **failover, not load balancing**: only one agent is active at a time.

selfCheck.q: After enabling sync, an admin tries to change a synced user's department in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Why does it fail, and where should the change be made?
selfCheck.a: The source of authority is now on-premises AD, so edit the attribute with on-premises AD tools and let it sync.

selfCheck.q: Contoso's AD uses the suffix contoso.local. What UPN do users get in Microsoft 365, and what should Contoso do?
selfCheck.a: Non-routable suffixes fall back to the onmicrosoft.com domain. Add a routable, verified UPN suffix, ideally matching the primary SMTP address.

selfCheck.q: A company acquired another firm whose forest has no network connectivity to its own. Which sync tool fits?
selfCheck.a: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync, with an agent deployed in each isolated forest.

modules.title: Implement directory synchronization tools
modules.learnSummary: This module examines the Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync installation requirements, the options for installing and configuring the tools, and how to monitor synchronization services using Microsoft Entra Connect Health.
modules.tldr: This module covers how to install Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync. Connect Sync needs a hardened Tier 0 Windows Server, a SQL database and either Express setup (single forest with PHS) or Custom setup for anything more advanced. You can add a staging server for resilience. Cloud Sync needs a gMSA, a cloud-only Hybrid Identity Administrator and lightweight provisioning agents that you configure in the Microsoft Entra admin center, and Microsoft Entra Connect Health monitors the sync infrastructure.
objectives: Configure Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync prerequisites.
Set up Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync.
Monitor synchronization services using Microsoft Entra Connect Health.
keyPoints: Only **one active Connect Sync server** per tenant. Extra servers run in **staging mode**: they import and sync but **don't export**, PHS and password writeback are off, and you promote one if the active server fails.
Connect Sync server: **Windows Server 2016+** (2022 recommended), **full GUI** (no Server Core), .NET 4.6.2+. It can be a DC, a member server or a non-domain-joined server.

Harden the sync server as a **Control Plane (Tier 0)** asset: restrict admin access, deny NTLM, use LAPS and PAWs, require MFA for privileged users, and **disable soft matching and hard match takeover**.

**Express setup** = single forest + **PHS** + automatic upgrade; it requires an **Enterprise Admin** account. **Custom setup** is for multiple forests, PTA/federation, a third-party IdP, filtering, writeback or an existing SQL Server/service account.
Selecting **Enable SSO** in Custom setup configures **PHS + PTA**, so PTA authenticates while on-premises AD is available and PHS is the fallback. Without it, only PHS is configured.

**Microsoft Entra Connect Health** (requires Microsoft Entra ID P1) monitors Connect Sync, AD FS and AD DS through agents. It gives alerts, email notifications for critical alerts, performance data and usage analytics.

Cloud Sync prerequisites: a **gMSA** (`provAgentgMSA$`), a **non-guest cloud-only Hybrid Identity Administrator** (prevents lockout), a Windows Server 2016+ host with 4 GB RAM and **outbound 443/80** (8080 optional).

Configure Cloud Sync in the Microsoft Entra admin center: **New configuration → AD to Microsoft Entra ID sync**. Then set scope and attribute mappings, test with **Provision a user**, set accidental-deletion protection and enable it.

units.title: Configure Microsoft Entra Connect Sync prerequisites
points: Verify the custom domain. The tenant object limit is 50,000 by default and 300,000 once the domain is verified; more than 500,000 needs a licence. Run IdFix first.

AD: schema and forest level 2003+, a writable DC (no RODC), no dotted NetBIOS names, Recycle Bin recommended. Use the RemoteSigned PowerShell execution policy and don't enable PowerShell transcription if the wizard manages AD FS.
Soft matching and hard match takeover let sync take over cloud-managed objects (overwriting data and password hashes), so disable them if you don't need them.
Staging servers support high availability, testing config changes, disaster recovery and migrations. Several staging servers can exist, but only one of them acts as the staging server at a time.

SQL: LocalDB 2019 Express (10 GB, about 100,000 objects) or full SQL Server up to 2022 with a `_CI_` collation and one sync engine per instance. Azure SQL isn't supported. TLS 1.2 is required from version 2.0.

units.title: Configure Microsoft Entra Connect Sync
points: Always download the latest setup program. Express setup installs the sync engine, configures the AD connector, enables PHS, optionally configures Exchange hybrid and enables automatic upgrade.
Custom-only options: custom install path, existing SQL Server, existing service account (needed with remote SQL) and custom local sync groups (Administrators, Operators, Browse, Password Reset).
Custom features: SSO method, multiple forests, matching across forests, OU filtering (good for pilots), source anchor (ImmutableID), sign-in attribute (Alternate ID) and Exchange hybrid.

More custom features: mail-enabled public folders (for DBEB), app and attribute filtering, password writeback (for SSPR), group writeback (needs Exchange on-premises), device writeback (Conditional Access) and directory extension attributes.
With existing AD FS, enabling SSO also lets the wizard configure AD FS (farm name, service account, TLS certificate). You can also enable staging mode during setup.

units.title: Monitor synchronization services using Microsoft Entra Connect Health
points: Agents on the monitored servers report to the Connect Health portal, which shows alerts, performance monitoring and usage analytics.
Connect Health for Sync: alerts, email for critical alerts and performance data. There are also separate views for AD FS and AD DS (forests, replication status).
Configure: enable agent auto-update, and optionally let Microsoft access health data for troubleshooting (off by default).

units.title: Configure Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync prerequisites
points: gMSA requirements: AD schema at Windows Server 2012+, RSAT PowerShell modules on a DC, at least one DC on 2012+ and an agent server on 2016+.
Create the cloud-only Hybrid Identity Administrator and add custom domains. Agent host: 4 GB RAM, .NET 4.7.1+ and the Undefined or RemoteSigned execution policy. Three active agents are recommended.
Ports: 443 for all outbound traffic, 80 for CRL downloads and 8080 (optional) for status reports every 10 minutes. NTLM must be disabled on the agent server.
Limits: group scope filtering for delta sync supports up to 50,000 members, and you can scope up to 59 separate OUs per configuration (nested OUs are fine). Renamed OUs or groups aren't detected.

units.title: Configure Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
points: Four tasks: install the provisioning agent, verify it in the admin center, verify it's running, then configure provisioning.

Download the agent from Microsoft Entra admin center → Hybrid management → Microsoft Entra Connect → Cloud Sync → Agents. The wizard asks for an extension (HR-driven provisioning or on-premises application provisioning).
For HR-driven provisioning, create or choose the gMSA, connect AD domains and optionally set DC priority.
Verify the agent shows as active on the Agents page and that the agent updater and provisioning agent services are Running on the server.
In the configuration, set the scope, manage attribute mappings, validate with Provision a user, set a notification email and accidental-deletion threshold, then Enable and Save.

keyTerms.definition: Connect Sync server that imports and syncs but exports nothing to Microsoft Entra ID; used for HA, testing and DR.
Default Connect Sync install: single forest, PHS, automatic upgrade.
Connect Sync install path for multiple forests, other sign-in methods, filtering, writeback, or existing SQL/service accounts.
Lets Connect Sync take over a cloud-managed object's source of authority; disable to prevent abuse.
Agent-based monitoring of Connect Sync, AD FS and AD DS with alerts and performance data.
Lightweight Cloud Sync agent on Windows Server that bridges on-premises AD and Microsoft Entra ID.

tables.title: Connect Sync: Express vs Custom setup
rows: PHS, PTA (PHS + PTA with SSO), AD FS federation, or none
Existing SQL Server and/or existing service account
OU filtering, app/attribute filtering, password/group/device writeback, directory extensions

remember: Second Connect Sync server for the same tenant → it must run in **staging mode**; two active servers aren't supported.
Need PTA, multiple forests or federation → choose **Custom** setup, not Express.
Cloud Sync lockout prevention → a **cloud-only** Hybrid Identity Administrator that isn't a guest.
Connect Sync can't be installed on **Server Core** and doesn't support **Azure SQL Database**.

selfCheck.q: You want a standby Connect Sync server that can take over quickly if the primary fails. How do you configure it?
selfCheck.a: Install it in staging mode. It imports and syncs without exporting, and you promote it if the active server fails.

selfCheck.q: A company with a single forest wants users to sign in with on-premises validation, falling back to PHS if on-premises AD is unavailable. Which setup option and setting?
selfCheck.a: Custom setup with the Enable SSO option, which configures both PTA and PHS.

selfCheck.q: Cloud Sync agents are behind a firewall. Which outbound ports must be open?
selfCheck.a: 443 for all service communication and 80 for CRL downloads. Port 8080 is optional for status reporting.

modules.title: Manage synchronized identities
modules.learnSummary: This module examines how to manage user identities when you configure Microsoft Entra Connect Sync, how to manage users and groups in Microsoft 365 with Microsoft Entra Connect Sync, and how to maintain directory synchronization.
modules.tldr: Once sync is running, you manage synced users and groups on-premises. The cloud keeps only a few settings, such as licences and advanced Exchange Online options. This module covers recovering deletes, writeback features, filtering, the built-in ADSync security groups and Microsoft Identity Manager, plus the tools to troubleshoot sync: Synchronization Service Manager, duplicate attribute resiliency, sync error views and the troubleshooter.
objectives: Ensure users synchronize efficiently.
Manage groups with directory synchronization.
Use Microsoft Entra Connect Sync Security Groups to help maintain directory synchronization.
Configure object filters for directory synchronization.
Explain how Microsoft Identity Manager helps organizations manage and synchronize user identities across their organizations and hybrid environments.
Troubleshoot directory synchronization using various troubleshooting tasks and tools.
keyPoints: Manage synced users and groups with **AD Users and Computers or on-premises PowerShell**. Only **licences** and advanced Exchange Online settings (e.g. In-place Archiving) are managed in the cloud.

Deleted synced users are **soft-deleted for 30 days**. Restore them in the Microsoft 365 admin center (Deleted users) or with `Restore-MgDirectoryDeletedItem`. A **hard delete (purge)** can't be undone.

**Password writeback** (Connect Sync and Cloud Sync) plus SSPR writes cloud password changes back to AD. **Device writeback** (Connect Sync only) writes devices to AD for AD FS-based Conditional Access.
**Group writeback** (Connect Sync) writes **Microsoft 365 groups** back to AD as **distribution groups**. It needs Exchange 2013 CU8+ and is prepared with `Initialize-ADSyncGroupWriteBack`.

Filtering options: **group, domain, OU and attribute** (attribute filtering is Connect Sync only). Multiple filters combine with a logical **AND**. Disable the scheduler (`Set-ADSyncScheduler -SyncCycleEnabled $False`) before changing filters.
**Prevent accidental deletes** stops exports with more than **500 deletions** by default. Users deleted by a filtering mistake can be restored, but other object types (e.g. security groups) can't.
**Duplicate attribute resiliency** quarantines duplicate UPN or SMTP ProxyAddress values instead of failing. A duplicate UPN gets a placeholder `prefix+4digits@tenant.onmicrosoft.com`.
Sync runs every **30 minutes** and password hashes every **2 minutes**. Force a sync with `Start-ADSyncSyncCycle -PolicyType Delta` (or `Initial` for a full sync).

units.title: Manage users with directory synchronization
points: Changes made to synced users in the Microsoft 365 admin center or Exchange admin center aren't synced back on-premises. A deleted user's licence becomes free to reassign.
If AD Recycle Bin is enabled, restoring an account there re-links it. Without it, you must create a new account with a new GUID.

Orphaned cloud objects (deletes that didn't sync): run a delta sync and verify it in Synchronization Service Manager. Then remove the object with `Remove-MgUser`, `Remove-MgContact` or `Remove-MgGroup` if needed.
Moving an out-of-sync user to another OU can make Connect Sync soft-delete the cloud account. Moving it back within 30 days reactivates it; otherwise it's permanently deleted.

Password writeback needs Windows Server 2008+ DCs, a Microsoft Entra ID premium licence and SSPR. Enable it in the Connect Sync wizard (Optional features) or with `Set-AADCloudSyncPasswordWritebackConfiguration` for Cloud Sync. Then enable it under Password reset → On-premises integration.

Device writeback needs devices and users in a single forest, a Windows Server 2012 R2+ forest and AD FS. Run the wizard a second time (Configure device options). Writeback can take up to 3 hours, and devices appear under RegisteredDevices.

units.title: Manage groups with directory synchronization
points: After sync, manage all group membership in on-premises AD.

Group writeback covers Microsoft 365 groups only, not security or distribution groups. Run `Update-Recipient`, `Update-AddressList` or `Update-GlobalAddressList` to show them in the on-premises GAL sooner.
Only members whose accounts were created on-premises are written back, and the group's name attribute is filled with its ObjectGUID.
Cloud Sync now supports group writeback in preview (from provisioning agent 1.1.1370.0).

units.title: Maintain directory synchronization using Microsoft Entra Connect Sync security groups
points: Setup creates the groups automatically. Use them to delegate control, grant temporary rights to run a manual sync, or troubleshoot.

ADSyncAdmins has full access; ADSyncOperators runs management agents, views statistics and saves run history; ADSyncBrowse gathers user lineage; ADSyncPasswordSet uses the password management interface.
Operators and PasswordSet members must also be members of ADSyncBrowse.
The groups are local groups on member servers and domain groups when installed on a DC. Use Specify Custom Sync Groups to get domain groups on a member server.

units.title: Configure object filters for directory synchronization
points: Microsoft recommends the default (sync all objects in all domains) for a complete GAL. Filter for pilots, service accounts or disabled accounts kept for compliance.
Group-based filtering must be configured at initial install. Domain and OU filtering can change later. Attribute-based filtering can differ per object type.
Filters are retained across upgrades (verify before the first sync), and with multiple forests you must apply them to each forest. Filtering out objects deletes them from Microsoft Entra ID.

After domain or OU filter changes, run a Full import followed by a Delta sync. After attribute filter changes, run a Full sync. Review staged exports in CSV before exporting, then re-enable the scheduler.

units.title: Explore Microsoft Identity Manager
points: MIM is primarily an on-premises identity management solution. It provides provisioning and deprovisioning, sync across AD, LDAP, SQL and apps, SSPR, lifecycle policies, RBAC, workflows and approvals, certificate and smart card management, and reporting.
Compared with Microsoft 365, MIM is on-premises, integrates with on-premises systems, is highly customizable and suits complex hybrid scenarios.
MIM puts the right users and access rights into AD, and Connect Sync or Cloud Sync then carries them to Microsoft Entra ID. MIM also helps protect privileged on-premises accounts.
The latest version is MIM 2016 2.0. Servers need Windows Server, SQL Server and SharePoint Server, plus the components: Synchronization Service and Service & Portal.

units.title: Troubleshoot directory synchronization
points: Typical causes: wrong credentials, sync accidentally deactivated, AD changes affecting OU or attribute scoping, a corrupted AD, and duplicate UPN or ProxyAddress values.
Deactivating sync moves the source of authority to Microsoft 365. Reactivating it moves authority back on-premises and overwrites cloud changes.

Quarantined conflicts are stored in DirSyncProvisioningErrors, and an hourly task releases resolved ones. View sync errors in the Microsoft 365 admin center (User management → Sync errors). Error report emails go to the technical contact.

The troubleshooter offers a Quick Scan (event logs and settings) or a Full Scan (adds AD objects) via the Microsoft 365 Support Assistant. Synchronization Service Manager → Operations shows import, export and sync results; under Connectors, choose Run with a Full, Delta or Export profile.

PHS issues: temporary passwords (User must change password at next logon) don't sync. A full password sync must be requested manually with PowerShell. If the object quota is exceeded, contact support.

keyTerms.definition: Deleted user kept in a deleted state for 30 days and restorable; the licence is freed.
Cloud object whose on-premises delete never synced; remove with Remove-MgUser/Contact/Group.
Writes Microsoft 365 groups back to on-premises AD as distribution groups.
ADSyncAdmins, ADSyncOperators, ADSyncBrowse and ADSyncPasswordSet, which delegate Connect Sync tasks.
Quarantines conflicting UPN or SMTP ProxyAddress values so the object still provisions.
Multi-valued attribute storing quarantined conflicting attributes.
On-premises identity lifecycle, sync and governance solution.

tables.title: Filtering options
rows: Configured at initial install; can slow large sync cycles
All object types in selected OUs
Different filters per object type possible

remember: Password writeback → **both** sync tools; device writeback → **Connect Sync only**.
Group writeback covers **Microsoft 365 groups** only, which arrive on-premises as **distribution groups**, not security groups.
**Reactivating** directory sync overwrites changes made in the cloud while it was off.
A user's password doesn't sync → check for **User must change password at next logon**; temporary passwords aren't synced.

selfCheck.q: A user deleted in AD (no AD Recycle Bin) synced to the cloud 10 days ago. How can you recover the cloud account?
selfCheck.a: It's soft-deleted for 30 days, so restore it in the Microsoft 365 admin center (Deleted users) or with Restore-MgDirectoryDeletedItem.

selfCheck.q: You need to change OU filtering safely in Connect Sync. What do you do first and what runs afterwards?
selfCheck.a: Disable the scheduler with Set-ADSyncScheduler -SyncCycleEnabled $False. After the change, run a Full import and a Delta sync, review the staged exports, export, then re-enable the scheduler.

selfCheck.q: Two on-premises users share the same UPN. What happens in Microsoft Entra ID?
selfCheck.a: Duplicate attribute resiliency quarantines the duplicate and gives the second user a placeholder UPN (prefix+4 digits@tenant.onmicrosoft.com).

paths.title: Manage identity and access in Microsoft 365
paths.summary: This learning path examines the threat vectors and data breaches organizations face today in their cybersecurity landscape, and the wide range of security solutions that Microsoft 365 provides to combat those threats.

modules.title: Examine threat vectors and data breaches
modules.learnSummary: This module examines the types of threat vectors and their potential outcomes that organizations must deal with on a daily basis and how users can enable hackers to access targets by unwittingly executing malicious content. MS-102
modules.tldr: Most attacks follow a kill chain, so you defend at every step. Email threats such as phishing, spoofing and malware lead to account breaches and elevation of privilege, and those in turn lead to data exfiltration, deletion or spillage. The module pairs each threat with the controls that mitigate it, especially MFA, few Global Administrators, least privilege, DLP, offline backups and an eDiscovery-driven spillage process.
objectives: Describe techniques hackers use to compromise user accounts through email.
Describe techniques hackers use to gain control over resources.
Describe techniques hackers use to compromise data.
Mitigate an account breach.
Prevent an elevation of privilege attack.
Prevent data exfiltration, data deletion, and data spillage.
keyPoints: Attacks follow a **kill chain**. Because attackers can bypass any single step, the best strategy puts defenses on **every step**.
**Phishing** lures users to fake sites or malware (viruses, Trojan horses, rootkits, spyware). **Spear phishing/whaling** targets executives.

**Spoofing** forges the sender. The **5321.MailFrom** (Return-Path) address can differ from the displayed **5322.From** address, and EOP **spoof intelligence** blocks illegitimate spoofing while allowing legitimate cases.

**Account breach** vectors: password attacks, phishing, credential stuffing, key loggers and social engineering. The main mitigations are **MFA** and **Microsoft Entra ID Protection**, and MFA is preferred over password expiration.
**Elevation of privilege**: attackers aim for Global Administrator, often by creating a new admin account to hide in plain sight. Keep **2–5 Global Administrators** and review them regularly.
**Data exfiltration** prevention: ACLs, external sharing policies, least privilege, **data classification** tiers and **Microsoft Purview DLP**.
**Data deletion** (including ransomware): Microsoft's built-in redundancy isn't enough, so **back up critical data to offline storage** and limit delete rights with RBAC.
**Data spillage**: use an **eDiscovery case** to search, review, trace and **permanently purge** the data, then rerun the search as proof of deletion.

units.title: Explore today's work and threat landscape
points: The kill chain is a step-wise attack pattern. Defend at choke points, and ideally at every step.
Data now lives on-premises, on PCs, on phones and in the cloud. MDM helps, but you have no control once data leaves the managed environment.
Many employees use unapproved apps and personal storage, and most breaches could be avoided with appropriate internal controls.

units.title: Examine how phishing retrieves sensitive information
points: Phishing emails look legitimate, convey urgency and link to look-alike sites that harvest credentials or deliver malware.
Malware payloads: viruses replicate into other programs; Trojan horses act as backdoors; rootkits give hidden admin access; spyware captures activity and keystrokes.
Spear phishing (whaling) targets specific high-profile individuals, usually for financial gain.

units.title: Examine how spoofing deceives users and compromises data security
points: SMTP lets a domain send as another domain. Legitimate uses include bulk-mail vendors, assistants sending on behalf of others, app notifications and mailing lists.
EOP (in Exchange Online or standalone) automatically protects inbound mail against spoofing with its single default spoof intelligence policy.
An attacker can set 5322.From to a trusted name (e.g. a bank) while the mail actually comes from their own 5321.MailFrom address.

units.title: Compare spam and malware
points: Spam and bulk mail are mostly a nuisance without a payload, but attackers use them to deliver malware.
Malware arrives as an attachment or a link. In stage 1 it exploits the computer using macros or JavaScript; in stage 2 it delivers the payload.
Even harmless-looking code can redirect a browser to a malicious site.

units.title: Examine account breaches
points: A breached admin account gives immediate access; a breached user account leads to elevation of privilege.

Mitigations: MFA, Microsoft Entra ID Protection (risk-based Conditional Access), strong unique passwords, awareness training, least privilege, monitoring and SIEM, patching, security testing and an incident response plan.
Password expiration offers no containment benefit because attackers use stolen credentials immediately, so Microsoft recommends MFA instead.
Protect data with encryption (TLS), DLP and Microsoft Purview Information Protection labels.

units.title: Examine elevation of privilege attacks
points: Attackers want Global Administrator, or service-specific privileges where the target data lives.
Prevention: Microsoft Entra MFA, especially for admins and accounts with access to sensitive content, plus 2–5 Global Administrators with regular reviews, auditing and alerts.
After a breach, look for new accounts, recent promotions, global configuration changes and data interactions. Check ACLs, mailbox delegates, forwarding rules and transport rules.

units.title: Examine how data exfiltration moves data out of your tenant
points: Motives: IP theft, blackmail, selling data and further entrenchment. Even directory information is useful to an attacker.
Protect accounts first (breach and elevation), then restrict access with ACLs reviewed regularly, external sharing restrictions and least privilege (View rather than Edit).
Classify data into risk tiers (high, medium or low business impact) and combine this with Microsoft Purview DLP, e.g. to block emailing credit card numbers externally. Add auditing and alerts.

units.title: Examine how attackers delete data from your tenant
points: Ransomware encrypts data and demands payment, and paying often leads to more targeting. Deletion can also cover tracks or cause harm.
Attackers can delete data from SharePoint sites and their recycle bins, so keep offline backups that you know how to restore.
Layer your controls: MFA, RBAC on delete rights, alerts, encryption, patching, Defender for Office 365, training, labels, an incident response plan and ending departing employees' sessions.

units.title: Examine how data spillage exposes data outside your tenant
points: Spillage means a confidential document has been released into an untrusted environment. Assess its scope, examine user activity and permanently purge it.

Steps: control case access (e.g. a Data Spillage Investigator role group) → create an eDiscovery case → search → review (preview a sample of 1,000; eDiscovery (Premium) can review 10,000) → message trace.
Message trace keeps 30 days of real-time and 90 days of historical data. Prepare mailboxes (single item recovery, holds) before purging.

Purging requires the Organization Management role group or the Search And Purge role. Rerun the search to verify, export a proof-of-deletion report and delete the search query, which may itself contain the spilled data.

units.title: Examine other types of attacks
points: Password cracking tries thousands of combinations. Microsoft Entra ID counters it with smart lockout; without Entra authentication, enable lockout controls in your own directory.
Malicious insiders know the company well and can be the most damaging, especially admins. They may create backdoor accounts, exfiltrate data or delete it.
Prevention: secure accounts, manage privileges, protect data, discern motives, identify unhappy employees, and use access controls and auditing for vendors and contingent staff.

keyTerms.definition: The step-by-step pattern an attack follows toward its goal.
Phishing aimed at specific, often senior, individuals.
EOP's default (and only) spoof policy that allows legitimate spoofing and blocks malicious spoofing.
The envelope sender (Return-Path) vs the From address shown in the mail client.
Using username/password pairs from other breaches to sign in elsewhere.
Unauthorized retrieval of data out of a computer or service.
A user releases a confidential document into an untrusted environment.

tables.title: Threats and key mitigations
rows: MFA, Microsoft Entra ID Protection, strong unique passwords, training, monitoring
MFA on admins, 2–5 Global Administrators, regular reviews, auditing and alerts
ACLs, external sharing policies, least privilege, data classification, Microsoft Purview DLP
MFA, RBAC on delete rights, alerts, offline backups, Defender for Office 365
eDiscovery case, message trace, Search and Purge, proof of deletion
Smart lockout (Microsoft Entra ID) or directory lockout controls

remember: Number of Global Administrators → **at least two, at most five**, for any tenant size.
Password expiration doesn't contain breaches → think **MFA**.
Microsoft 365 redundancy isn't a backup → keep **offline backups** of critical data.
Spillage clean-up ends with **rerunning the search** (no results) and **deleting the query**, because the query can contain the spilled data.

selfCheck.q: An attacker compromised a user and promoted a new, unused account to Global Administrator. What preventive controls does the module recommend?
selfCheck.a: MFA, especially for admins, plus keeping Global Administrators to two to five and regularly reviewing them and their activity.

selfCheck.q: A user emailed a highly confidential file to many internal and external recipients. Which tool drives the clean-up, and which role is needed to purge?
selfCheck.a: An eDiscovery case for search, review and proof of deletion. Purging requires the Organization Management role group or the Search And Purge role.

selfCheck.q: Which header address does the recipient see as the sender in a spoofed email?
selfCheck.a: The 5322.From address; the real sending address is the 5321.MailFrom (Return-Path).

modules.title: Explore the Zero Trust security model
modules.learnSummary: This module examines the concepts and principles of the Zero Trust security model, as well as how Microsoft 365 supports it, and how your organization can implement it. MS-102
modules.tldr: Zero Trust treats every request as if it came from an open network: never trust, always verify. It rests on three principles (verify explicitly, least privileged access, assume breach) applied across six foundational elements, with Microsoft Entra Conditional Access as its policy engine. Organizations secure identity in five steps and adopt Zero Trust across identity, security, compliance and skilling.
objectives: Describe the Zero Trust approach to security in Microsoft 365.
Describe the principles and components of the Zero Trust security model.
Describe the five steps to implementing a Zero Trust security model in your organization.
Explain Microsoft's story and strategy around Zero Trust networking.
keyPoints: Zero Trust = **never trust, always verify**. Every request is fully authenticated, authorized and encrypted, whatever its origin.
Three principles: **verify explicitly** (all data points), **least privileged access** (JIT/JEA, risk-based policies) and **assume breach** (segment, encrypt end to end, use analytics).
Six foundational elements: **identities, endpoints, applications, data, infrastructure, networks**. Each is a signal source, an enforcement control plane and a resource to defend.
Five steps to secure identity: **strengthen credentials**, **reduce attack surface**, **automate threat response**, **increase awareness**, **enable user self-help**.
Move from **implicit trust** (being on the network) to **explicit verification** of authentication claims, devices and data. Assess session risk from user, device state, apps and data sensitivity.

**Microsoft Entra Conditional Access** (with ID Protection) is the policy engine. It allows, blocks or restricts access based on user, device, location, app and sign-in risk, and can require MFA or terms of use.
A Zero Trust network replaces perimeter trust with signals from an **identity provider**, a **device directory**, a **policy evaluation service** and an **access proxy**.
The **Zero Trust Assessment tool** shows your maturity stage (**Traditional, Advanced, Optimal**) and how to reach the next one.

units.title: Examine the principles and components of the Zero Trust model
points: Zero Trust uses microsegmentation and least privilege to limit lateral movement, plus analytics to detect anomalies in real time.
Identities are the control plane: verify them with strong authentication. Endpoints: enforce device health and compliance.
Apps: discover shadow IT and control in-app permissions and actions. Data: classify, label and encrypt it so it stays protected outside your control.
Infrastructure: assess version and configuration and use JIT access. Networks: segment, use real-time threat protection and end-to-end encryption.
Shift from trust-by-default to trust-by-exception, with automated management of exceptions and alerts.

units.title: Plan for a Zero Trust security model in your organization
points: Assume everything is on the open internet. The idea that being on the network means it's OK fails against insiders and phishing.

Five identity steps: strengthen credentials (MFA), reduce attack surface (drop legacy protocols, limit admin access), automate threat response, increase awareness (auditing and logging) and enable user self-help.

Holistic policies allow, block or restrict access, e.g. with MFA, limited downloads or terms of use. They stop stolen credentials on unknown devices and verified users reaching data they shouldn't see.
The Zero Trust Assessment tool covers identities, devices, apps, infrastructure, network and data.

units.title: Examine Microsoft's strategy for Zero Trust networking
points: Network objectives: be ready before attacks happen, minimize damage and spread, and make your cloud footprint harder to compromise. Perimeter-based defense is obsolete.
Dynamic trust lets some assets be reached from any device while high-value assets require managed, compliant devices.
Initial objectives: cloud micro-perimeters with some micro-segmentation, cloud-native filtering of known threats, and encrypted user-to-app traffic.
Next objectives: fully distributed micro-perimeters with deeper micro-segmentation, ML-based threat protection with context signals, and encryption of all traffic.
Baseline Conditional Access policies enforce MFA in high-risk scenarios, on by default in report-only mode. Security Defaults showed up to 80% fewer compromises.

units.title: Adopt a Zero Trust approach
points: Identity is the starting point. Passwordless options include Windows Hello for Business, Microsoft Authenticator and FIDO2 keys; a Temporary Access Pass bootstraps or recovers them. Add Conditional Access with authentication context, and verifiable credentials.
Security: unified investigation in the Microsoft Defender portal, shared incidents between Defender XDR and Microsoft Sentinel, Threat Analytics reports and Secured-core servers and devices.
Compliance (inside-out protection): coauthoring of protected documents, Insider Risk Management, DLP for Chrome and on-premises file shares/SharePoint Server, and Purview labels across other clouds.
Skilling: certifications include Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals; Information Protection Administrator; Security Operations Analyst; and Identity and Access Administrator.

keyTerms.definition: Authenticate and authorize using all data points: identity, location, device health, workload, data classification, anomalies.
Just-in-time and just-enough-access plus risk-based adaptive policies.
Minimize blast radius through segmentation, end-to-end encryption and analytics.
Dividing networks into small zones to block lateral movement.
Component of a Zero Trust network that grants or denies access using identity, device and policy signals.
Shows Zero Trust maturity (Traditional, Advanced, Optimal) with recommendations.

tables.title: Zero Trust network deployment objectives
rows: Many ingress/egress cloud micro-perimeters, some micro-segmentation
Machine learning-based protection with context signals

remember: Zero Trust principles are **verify explicitly, least privileged access, assume breach**. Implicit trust and most-privileged access are distractors.
The policy engine of Microsoft's Zero Trust solution is **Microsoft Entra Conditional Access**.
Being on the corporate network proves nothing → verify **authentication, device and data** explicitly.

selfCheck.q: Which Zero Trust principle is about segmenting access and encrypting sessions end to end to limit blast radius?
selfCheck.a: Assume breach.

selfCheck.q: An admin wants to allow access from any device to low-value apps but only from compliant devices to finance data. Which capability enables this?
selfCheck.a: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, which makes dynamic access decisions on device compliance and other signals.

selfCheck.q: Name two of the five steps to securing your identity infrastructure.
selfCheck.a: Any two of: strengthen credentials, reduce attack surface, automate threat response, increase awareness, enable user self-help.

modules.title: Manage secure user access in Microsoft 365
modules.learnSummary: This module examines the various features provided in the Microsoft 365 ecosystem for securing user access, such as Conditional Access policies, multifactor authentication, self-service password management, Smart Lockout policies, and security defaults.
modules.tldr: This module covers how to secure sign-in to Microsoft 365. It starts with password management and Microsoft Entra Password Protection, then MFA through security defaults, Conditional Access or (legacy) per-user settings. Conditional Access (Microsoft Entra ID P1) is the main policy engine. PTA, passwordless methods, SSPR, Smart Lockout and the sign-in logs complete the toolkit.
objectives: Manage user passwords.
Create Conditional Access policies.
Enable security defaults.
Describe pass-through authentication.
Enable multifactor authentication.
Describe self-service password management.
Implement Microsoft Entra Smart Lockout.
keyPoints: Default policy: passwords **never expire** (recommended). If you set expiry, it must be **14–730 days**. Microsoft recommends **MFA instead of periodic changes**.

**Password Protection**: the **global banned list** is always on and can't be disabled. The **custom banned list** holds up to **1,000 terms** of 4–16 characters, so ban base terms and the algorithm blocks their variants.

**Conditional Access** is an if-then policy evaluated **after first-factor authentication**. It needs **Microsoft Entra ID P1** (or Business Premium/E3) and uses signals such as users, location, device, app and risk to block or grant access with controls.

Three ways to enable MFA: **security defaults** (all-or-nothing, free), **Conditional Access** (recommended, granular) or **legacy per-user MFA** (not recommended). Security defaults and Conditional Access are **mutually exclusive**.

**Security defaults**: MFA registration within **14 days**, MFA for admins and Azure management, MFA for users when needed, and **legacy authentication blocked**. Tenants created on or after 22 October 2019 have them on by default.
**Authentication strength** requires specific method combinations. The built-in strengths are **MFA**, **passwordless MFA** and **phishing-resistant MFA**; you can also create custom ones.

**Smart Lockout** (always on): locks for **60 seconds after 10 failures** by default and won't count the **same bad password** repeatedly. With PTA, keep the Entra threshold **below** the AD threshold and the Entra lockout duration **longer** than the AD reset counter.
**SSPR** is off by default. Hybrid users need **Microsoft Entra ID P1/P2 plus password writeback**. Admins must use **two methods** and **no security questions**.

units.title: Examine the identity and access tools used in Microsoft 365
points: Microsoft Entra ID supports cloud-only, hybrid and federated identity models and many authentication methods, and it enforces Conditional Access, Identity Protection, PIM and access reviews.
The Microsoft 365 admin center manages users, groups, licences, billing, security and settings, and uses Microsoft Entra ID for authentication.
SSO works for gallery apps, for on-premises apps (via Application Proxy, Connect Sync or AD FS) and over SAML, OAuth, OpenID Connect and WS-Federation.
Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK and the Microsoft Graph API give granular, scriptable, consistent access to Microsoft 365 data.

units.title: Manage user passwords
points: Global, Security and Privileged Role Administrators can do all password tasks. User and Password Administrators can reset passwords. Set expiry in Settings → Org settings → Security & privacy.

Only another Global Administrator can reset a Global Administrator's password. Self-reset via Can't access your account? needs an alternate email (and a phone if you use a custom domain or sync) and must finish within 10 minutes.
The global banned list comes from Microsoft Entra telemetry, not third-party breach lists, and isn't published. Use fuzzy matching and ban base terms (e.g. Fabrikam, London).

Configure it in Microsoft Entra admin center → Protection → Authentication methods → Password protection: Enforce custom list = Yes. If Enable password protection on Windows Server AD is set to No, DC agents go quiescent. Updates can take hours.
Licensing: the global list is Free for cloud-only users. A custom list, or any use for synced users, needs P1/P2.

units.title: Implement Conditional Access policies
points: Defender for Endpoint provides device risk, Intune deploys compliance policies, and Conditional Access blocks devices above the threat level. It supports device-based and app-based Conditional Access.

Assignments are users (including guests and directory roles), target resources (apps, user actions, authentication context), network and conditions. Named locations allow up to 195 locations with 2,000 IP ranges each and CIDR masks greater than /8. Use IP ranges rather than countries to trust a single office.

Grant controls: block, or require MFA, authentication strength, a compliant device, a hybrid-joined device, an approved client app, an app protection policy or a password change. All selected controls are required by default.

Session controls: app-enforced restrictions, Conditional Access App Control (via Defender for Cloud Apps), sign-in frequency, persistent browser, continuous access evaluation, resilience defaults and token protection.

Test with report-only mode and the What If tool before enabling Block policies. When several authentication-strength policies apply, the user must satisfy all of them, and users without a qualifying method are sent to combined registration.

units.title: Enable pass-through authentication
points: PTA validates passwords against on-premises AD without storing them in the cloud. It's a simpler alternative to AD FS for organizations that need on-premises authentication, and it can fail over to PHS.

Flow: the credentials go onto the connector queue, an on-premises agent validates them against AD, and the result returns to Microsoft Entra ID. Communication is outbound only, so there's no need for the perimeter network.
Enable it in the Connect Sync wizard (User sign-in → Pass-through authentication). The first agent runs on the Connect Sync server; add at least one more for high availability and load balancing.

units.title: Implement multifactor authentication
points: Factors are something you know, something you own and something you are. Methods: phone call or text (the default), Microsoft Authenticator, OATH hardware tokens, FIDO2 keys and third-party TOTP apps.
By licence: all plans can use security defaults; Business Premium, E3 or P1 can use Conditional Access; E5 or P2 can use risk-based policies with Identity Protection.
Turn off per-user MFA and security defaults before enabling Conditional Access. Recommended policies: MFA for admins, MFA for all users and blocking legacy authentication.

Per-user MFA (Settings → Org settings → Multifactor authentication) doesn't block legacy protocols and lacks context. Service settings control app passwords, trusted IPs, verification options and remembered devices (1–365 days, default 90).
Prefer Conditional Access sign-in frequency over the remember-MFA setting. Too many prompts make users approve malicious prompts.

units.title: Explore passwordless authentication options
points: Windows Hello for Business: a TPM-backed, device-bound PIN or biometric credential for dedicated Windows PCs, with SSO to on-premises and cloud resources.
macOS: Platform Credential (Secure Enclave key, Touch ID, phishing-resistant) and Platform SSO with smart card (needs CBA, configured via Intune or another MDM).

Microsoft Authenticator offers phone sign-in with number matching and biometric or PIN confirmation. Push notifications are preferred over TOTP. Enable combined registration first, then enable users for the method.
Passkeys (FIDO2) are unphishable USB, NFC or Bluetooth keys, ideal for shared PCs, kiosks or users who can't use a phone.
Certificate-based authentication uses X.509 certificates directly against Microsoft Entra ID with no AD FS. It's free and phishing-resistant.

units.title: Explore self-service password management
points: Enable SSPR for all users or specific groups. Methods: alternate email, office phone, mobile call or text, and security questions.
Users start a reset with Can't access your account? on the sign-in page. Microsoft Support can't reset forgotten passwords.
Without writeback, SSPR works only for cloud identities. Hybrid users need P1/P2 plus Connect Sync password writeback.

units.title: Implement Microsoft Entra Smart Lockout
points: Smart Lockout distinguishes genuine users (familiar locations) from attackers with separate counters. Each datacenter tracks lockouts independently.
It tracks the last three bad password hashes, but not with PTA, because validation happens on-premises. Lockout duration grows with repeated lockouts.

Customizing the threshold or duration (Protection → Authentication methods → Password protection) needs paid licences. Locked users can unlock themselves with SSPR, but admins must wait for the lockout to expire.

units.title: Explore Security Defaults in Microsoft Entra ID
points: Designed for Free-tier tenants and organizations without Conditional Access. MFA plus blocking legacy authentication stops more than 99.9% of identity attacks.
Enable it under Microsoft Entra admin center → Overview → Properties → Manage security defaults (Security, Conditional Access or Global Administrator).

Admin roles such as Global, Exchange, SharePoint, Security, User, Helpdesk and Password Administrator must use MFA at every sign-in. Azure Resource Manager access (portal, PowerShell, CLI) requires MFA for everyone.
Registration is via Authenticator notifications or OATH TOTP apps, so don't disable authentication methods. The Connect Sync account is excluded, and B2B users are treated like your own users.
Keep at least two emergency access Global Administrator accounts with long, complex passwords stored offline.

units.title: Investigate authentication issues using sign-in logs
points: The Microsoft Entra admin center has three activity logs: sign-in, audit (tenant changes) and provisioning.
Sign-in logs come in four types: interactive user, non-interactive user, service principal and managed identity. Classic logs show only interactive sign-ins, and entries can't be edited or deleted.
Interactive logs show location and whether Conditional Access applied. Non-interactive sign-ins (token refresh, SSO) are grouped when app, user, IP, status and resource match.
Service principal sign-ins use certificates or secrets. Managed identity sign-ins come from Azure resources whose secrets Azure manages.

keyTerms.definition: Up to 1,000 organization-specific base terms combined with the global banned list.
Microsoft Entra ID P1 policy engine: if these signals apply, then block or grant access with controls.
Conditional Access control that defines which authentication method combinations satisfy access.
Free, preconfigured baseline: MFA for everyone and legacy authentication blocked.
Locks out attackers after failed attempts while letting genuine users from familiar locations continue.
Conditional Access evaluates and logs policies without enforcing them.
A background token refresh or SSO done by a client on the user's behalf.

tables.title: Ways to enable MFA
rows: Also blocks legacy auth; can't coexist with Conditional Access
Business Premium, E3/E5, Microsoft Entra ID P1/P2
Per user, group, app, location, device, risk
Not recommended; doesn't block legacy authentication

remember: Want Conditional Access but security defaults are on → **disable security defaults first**; the two are mutually exclusive.
Trust only your Paris office → a named location with **IP ranges**, not **Countries/regions** (that would trust all of France).
A Global Administrator forgot their password → only **another Global Administrator** can reset it.
PTA plus Smart Lockout → Entra threshold **lower** than AD, Entra lockout duration **longer** than AD's reset counter.

selfCheck.q: A small business on Microsoft 365 Business Standard with no Entra ID P1 wants MFA for everyone and legacy authentication blocked. What should it enable?
selfCheck.a: Security defaults.

selfCheck.q: Fabrikam wants to block passwords like Fabrikam!1 and LondonHQ. What should it add to the custom banned password list?
selfCheck.a: Only the base terms (e.g. Fabrikam, London, Widget). The fuzzy-matching algorithm blocks the variants.

selfCheck.q: Before enforcing a new Conditional Access block policy, how can an admin see its impact safely?
selfCheck.a: Set the policy to report-only mode (and/or use the What If tool), then review the Conditional Access and Report-only tabs in the sign-in logs.

modules.title: Explore security solutions in Microsoft Defender XDR
modules.learnSummary: This module introduces you to several features in Microsoft 365 that can help protect your organization against cyberthreats, detect when a user or computer has been compromised, and monitor your organization for suspicious activities. MS-102
modules.tldr: Microsoft Defender XDR brings together the Microsoft 365 security workloads. Exchange Online Protection is the email baseline, and Defender for Office 365 adds Safe Attachments, Safe Links and (in Plan 2) investigation tools. Defender for Identity watches on-premises AD signals, Defender for Endpoint protects devices, Threat Intelligence and Defender for Cloud Apps add visibility, and the Microsoft Defender portal provides the reports.
objectives: Identify the features of Microsoft Defender for Office 365 that enhance email security in a Microsoft 365 deployment
Explain how Microsoft Defender for Identity identifies, detects, and investigates advanced threats, compromised identities, and malicious insider actions directed at your organization
Explain how Microsoft Defender for Endpoint helps enterprise networks prevent, detect, investigate, and respond to advanced threats
Describe how Microsoft 365 Threat Intelligence can be beneficial to your organization’s security officers and administrators
Describe how Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps enhances visibility and control over your Microsoft 365 tenant through three core areas
keyPoints: **EOP** is included with every Exchange Online mailbox and also comes standalone. Its order is **connection filtering → malware → policy (mail flow rules) → content filtering**, then the verdict action.
**Defender for Office 365** extends EOP against zero-day threats. **Safe Attachments** detonates attachments in a hypervisor sandbox, and **Safe Links** gives **time-of-click** URL protection.

**Plan 1** = Safe Attachments, Safe Links (also for SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams), anti-phishing and real-time detections. **Plan 2** adds Threat Trackers, **Threat Explorer**, AIR, **attack simulation training** and hunting and incidents in Defender XDR.

**Defender for Identity** (formerly Azure ATP) uses **on-premises AD signals** and DC sensors. It detects reconnaissance, compromised credentials, lateral movement (Pass-the-Hash/Ticket) and domain dominance (Golden Ticket, DCShadow), and shows **Lateral Movement Paths**.

**Defender for Endpoint** combines endpoint behavioral sensors, cloud security analytics and threat intelligence. Its pillars are vulnerability management, **attack surface reduction**, **next-generation protection** (Defender Antivirus), **EDR**, **AIR** and **Secure Score for Devices**.

**Defender for Cloud Apps** has three core areas: **threat detection**, **enhanced control** and **discovery and insights**. **Cloud Discovery** maps the cloud apps in use (shadow IT) across more than 16,000 SaaS apps.
**Microsoft 365 Threat Intelligence** (E5 or an add-on) provides the Threat dashboard and Threat explorer, fed by the Microsoft Intelligent Security Graph.

Defender portal reports come in three categories: **Security**, **Email & collaboration** and **Endpoints**. Viewing them requires Organization Management, Security Administrator, Security Reader or Global Reader.

units.title: Enhance Exchange Online Protection with Microsoft Defender for Office 365
points: EOP techniques: IP, URL and domain reputation; spam, malware, content and connection filtering; and spoof intelligence. Connection filtering stops most spam.

Malware goes to quarantine, which only admins can access by default. Quarantine policies define what users can do. Content filtering verdicts: spam, high-confidence spam, phishing, high-confidence phishing, bulk and spoofing.
Defender for Office 365 targets zero-day malware, phishing campaigns and malicious URLs. Policies can be set per user, recipient, domain or organization and should be reviewed regularly.

Spoof intelligence (Email & collaboration → Policies & rules → Threat policies → Anti-spam) lets you allow or block senders that spoof your domains. Anti-phishing uses machine learning plus impersonation detection.
Threat Explorer gives real-time threat reporting. Attack simulation training covers spear-phishing credential harvest, attachments, password spray and brute force.

units.title: Protect your organization's identities using Microsoft Defender for Identity
points: Builds a behavioral baseline per user and flags anomalies. Proprietary sensors on domain controllers monitor activity from every device.
Reduces the attack surface with security reports, Lateral Movement Paths and reports on clear-text password authentication. It also protects AD FS.
Kill-chain detections: reconnaissance, compromised credentials, lateral movement and domain dominance.
Shows alerts on an attack timeline for fast triage and integrates with Defender for Endpoint.

units.title: Protect your enterprise network against advanced threats using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
points: Endpoint behavioral sensors in Windows 10/11 send signals to the organization's private, isolated cloud instance of Defender for Endpoint.
Threat and vulnerability management finds vulnerabilities in real time without agents or scans and ranks them by threat landscape and business context.

Attack surface reduction includes ASR rules, hardware-based isolation, application control, exploit protection, network protection, web protection, controlled folder access (ransomware) and the firewall.
EDR groups related alerts into incidents, and advanced hunting allows custom queries. AIR remediates automatically, with pending and completed actions tracked in the Action center.
Secure Score for Devices covers application, OS, network, accounts and security controls. Microsoft Threat Experts provides managed hunting: targeted attack notifications and experts on demand.

units.title: Protect against cyber attacks using Microsoft 365 Threat Intelligence
points: Included in Microsoft 365 E5 and available as an add-on for other Enterprise plans. It integrates with EOP and Defender for Office 365.
Uses the Microsoft Intelligent Security Graph and data from 3,500 security specialists, and shows daily threats detected, messages scanned and threats stopped.
The Threat dashboard gives CISOs global visibility. Threat explorer shows threat families, global threats and top targeted users.
Investigate malware by filtering on sender, recipient, IP and the detection technology that stopped it (EOP vs Defender for Office 365), and see every user who received it.

units.title: Provide insight into suspicious activity using Microsoft Defender for Cloud App Security
points: Threat detection, e.g. an alert when an admin unusually forwards mail. Enhanced control, e.g. an alert on a mass download. Discovery and insights show which apps are used and whether they're approved.
Deployment modes: log collection, API connectors and reverse proxy.

Framework: discover and control shadow IT (16,000+ apps assessed against 80+ risks), protect sensitive information, detect threats and anomalies such as ransomware or rogue apps, and assess compliance.
Tools: Cloud Discovery, sanctioning or unsanctioning apps, app connectors, Conditional Access App Control and continuous policy tuning.

units.title: Review the security reports in Microsoft Defender XDR
points: Security reports cover identities (users at risk, Global Admins), data (DLP matches), devices (at risk, malware, compliance) and apps (privileged OAuth apps, discovered apps).
Endpoint reports: threat protection, device health and compliance, vulnerable devices and web protection.
Email & collaboration reports include top malware, mail latency, threat protection status, URL protection, spoof detections, compromised users and user-reported messages.
Assigning the matching Microsoft Entra role grants Defender portal permissions.

keyTerms.definition: Built-in cloud email filtering for spam, malware, phishing and spoofing.
Defender for Office 365 feature that detonates unknown attachments in a sandbox to catch zero-day malware.
Time-of-click scanning of URLs in email and documents.
Defender for Identity view of how an attacker could move to sensitive accounts.
Defender for Endpoint capabilities (ASR rules, controlled folder access, etc.) that minimize exploitable areas.
Automated investigation and response/remediation; actions tracked in the Action center.
Defender for Cloud Apps feature that maps the cloud apps in use (shadow IT).

tables.title: Defender for Office 365 plans
rows: Safe Attachments, Safe Links, Safe Attachments for SharePoint/OneDrive/Teams, anti-phishing, real-time detections
Plan 1 + Threat Trackers, Threat Explorer, automated investigation and response, attack simulation training, advanced hunting, incidents and alerts in Defender XDR

tables.title: Which Defender workload?
rows: Windows behavioral sensors and cloud analytics

remember: Time-of-click URL protection → **Safe Links**; unknown attachment sandboxing → **Safe Attachments**.
Threat Explorer and attack simulation training → **Defender for Office 365 Plan 2**, not Plan 1.
Pass-the-Hash or Golden Ticket detection on on-premises AD → **Defender for Identity**, not Defender for Endpoint.
Discovering unsanctioned cloud apps → **Cloud Discovery** in Defender for Cloud Apps.

selfCheck.q: Users keep clicking links that only turn malicious after the email is delivered. Which feature helps?
selfCheck.a: Safe Links in Defender for Office 365, which checks URLs at the time of click.

selfCheck.q: A SOC wants to run phishing simulations against employees. Which plan is required?
selfCheck.a: Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, which includes attack simulation training.

selfCheck.q: Which Defender for Endpoint feature helps stop ransomware from changing files in key folders?
selfCheck.a: Controlled folder access, part of attack surface reduction (it requires Microsoft Defender Antivirus).

modules.title: Examine Microsoft  Secure Score
